## 2026-10-23 — The advisor draw reads origin, not a checkout 37 commits behind; the new tier's point refits to about USD 10, and the pace runs normal to the Monday 03:00 reset

<!-- head: 82f4b20bcbed -->

*Seat executor, 23 Oct 2026. Drawn at lane 0: `the-advisor-rung-reads-origin-and-the-pace-is-held`.*

**What was wrong.** The advisor rung listed `docs/staging/advisor/` from the disk of whichever checkout drew it. The shared checkout was 37 commits behind origin. So every draw there re-offered the other-pages steer, which origin had already moved to `done/`, as "REFUSED: not on origin". It also never saw two usage readings and two steers that origin carried. The authority check already demanded origin's bytes, so the listing was the only part reading the wrong tree. `scan` now lists origin/main's top level with `git ls-tree` and reads each file with `git show`. A disk-only file is still named as refused, so a forged file stays visible, unless origin holds it in `done/`. The control covers the whole partition in one folder: a file offered from origin though absent from disk, a stale top-level copy of a done file that stays silent, and a disk-only file refused. Both mutations fire (list the disk; drop the done exclusion). Run against the shared tree, the new draw shows exactly origin's five files.

**The fit.** The 13:44 value of USD 7.9 a point was the 06:55–09:45 interval. The 09:45–15:20 refit is USD 12.7 (10.2–16.9), and the pooled value is 10.3 (9.1–11.7). I cannot yet say why the afternoon point cost more; carry the pooled figure until the next reading.

**The pace.** The reset reading (15:31: "It's still Monday 03:00") had already replaced the item's "hold 0.7" with about 1.4 points an hour. The dial's fastest word is `normal`, so it is set until 2026-10-26T03:00Z. To reverse it: `python3 -m background.tick_mode slow --until 2026-10-26T03:00Z`. The reading asked for a reset constant to be corrected, but none exists in the code.

**Switched on under the new standing rule: the bill estimate reads the annualised advance.** It is the first switch-on under the director's 23 Oct ruling ("Great. All good. Do these."), now canon G9. An unread month is billed from the annual rate the account's own register advance implies, not from the last three reads. The rule was fixed before the arms ran, and the arms at 30674a4bd met it. Once the default flipped, a flag-less control arm would have run with the switch on but been labelled as the three-read estimate. It now stamps what ran. ## 2026-10-23 — Explore opens on eight households seen three ways, chosen by rule at publish; the rules find standard-variable bills above the cap

<!-- head: 17eaac83d063 -->

**In plain English:** Explore now opens on eight households, one per thing the supplier does. Each is picked by a rule every time the site is published, and you can step through its life and see each moment three ways: what the customer saw, what the supplier knew that day, and what was really true. Two of the eight could not be filled, and the page says why. Running the rules turned up a real problem: many standard-tariff bills are above the price cap.

*Worker tick, lane 0, 23 Oct 2026. The report the director's 23 Oct Explore steer asks for.*

**The cast rules, and which filled on the 19 Oct run (6 of 8).** Switch-in: the most recent joiner with a full first quarter (PROS-2025-0022). Renewal: the widest stored-belief-versus-truth gap at a retention decision (SYN-2016-441, 100% held against the truth). Estimate trap: the longest estimated run on one fuel ending in a catch-up (OCC-49cf03d82fea, 34 bills, then £532.80 credited). Debt: the deepest arrears journey (PROS-2021-0362, from a miss to the agency). EV home: the largest EV usage move (PROS-2021-0219). 2022 shock: the largest year-on-year rise in one month's bill (PROS-2017-0336, £440.53 to £1,402.76). Empty and saying so on the page: the mover (no move-out event, and new occupants are not linked to the old) and storage heating (no bill has two registers).

**Coverage findings**, all in `SEAT_FINDING_EXPLORES_CAST_FINDS_STANDARD_VARIABLE_BILLS_ABOVE_THE_CAP_AND_NO_MOVER_OR_TWO_RATE_HOME_2026-10-23.md`. 4,764 of 14,012 bills that can only be standard variable are above min(Ofgem cap, EPG) all-in, in 199 of 550 households and in every capped year. The 1 Oct fix `592596b44` is already in this run, so this is new. The cause is not attributed yet; four explanations are ranked in the finding, and the first to rule out is my own population reading. The EV home's car moved its use only +8%.

**The three mock-up checks.** (1) 306's November 2022 bills charge exactly the Ofgem cap (51.89p and 14.76p all-in), not the EPG: the guarantee never reached the bill. (2) The actual reads do land through catch-ups, but billed gas fell 8%, not the stated 24%; an untested explanation is a winter-against-spring average in the effect line. (3) The 2019 debt had two notices, then nothing for five years, then a write-off 13 days after leaving: the 27 Sep write-off finding, still live.

**No look-ahead.** Supplier rows are built only from records dated on or before the moment, each carrying `drawn_from`. A control reds on any later date, and it is mutation-proven: handing the supplier view the whole record is caught.

**Mistakes worth keeping.** I first wrote the cap check against "within a year of a renewal = fixed". It counted 271 households, and the run records no term length. Narrowing to before the first renewal, which can only be standard variable, cut that to 199 and is the honest population. The switch-in rule first picked a household with 11 days of bills, because "three invoices" counted both fuels together. The cold read caught a third: the renewal-decision moment showed that same day's outcome ("RENEWED") and the new fixed tariff in the supplier column. The run dates both on the same day, so "on or before" let them through. The decision moment now reads the record as it stood before its outcome, and a mutation-proven control holds it there.

**Cold-reader pass (one fresh Sonnet reader, given only the rendered text, reading twice).** *Energy reader, 4/10:* a sound device for showing what the supplier could not see. Bills above the cap read as a compliance failure presented as a quirk, which is the finding working as intended; the flag line is meant to make it unmissable. The reader also caught three wording faults, now fixed: "your fixed tariff is ending" shown to a household on standard variable, a credit printed as a negative bill, and a gap strip calling billed estimates "the truth". *Tech reader, 6/10:* the idea is clear and the open "6 of 8" reads as honest, but the jargon is heavy (PROS/OCC/SYN ids, "catch-up", "profile class 2", "resentment score"); a one-line glossary per tab is the change it most wants. Still open from the read: £/MWh tariff units, and "100%" in the company log against "99.9%" in the supplier panel. Also still owed: wiring the checks into Monday's step, and rendering the customer view from `company/portal/templates/`.

## 2026-10-23 — Section 14's four-seed grade: neither per-customer retention switch clears its departure interval, so both stay off

<!-- head: 4e9c7a524a51 -->

**In plain English:** We tested twice, on four sets of dice, whether tailoring each customer's retention offer to what the company believes about them creates value against a supplier that treats everyone alike. Neither version passed the test we set before the runs: on this book, any value they create is too small to tell apart from chance. Both stay switched off.

*Seat executor, 23 Oct 2026. Section 14 of `docs/staging/records/SEAT_PREREG_THE_PER_CUSTOMER_SWITCHES_ON_TOGETHER_AGAINST_FLAT_2026-10-21.md`, seed 5 graded and the four-seed grade (seeds 2 to 5) written under the rule fixed on 22 Oct before any seeded arm ran.*

**The result.** Seed 5 is valid (P14a′: 125 events differ from seed 1). Across the four seeds, the ending-term belief nets +£1,556 ± £2,104 against flat, and its `departure` channel nets +£3,618 ± £4,924. That channel is positive on every seed, but its interval contains zero. The save-odds guard nets +£367 ± £1,707, with `departure` at +£614 ± £3,289. The rule needs `departure` above zero AND net at least 0, so **neither switch is proposed. As the rule says: across these draws, on this book, the per-customer retention offers create no value that can be detected.** Under the director's 23 Oct ruling, point 3, a refuted rule leaves the switch off on the same record, with the reason. Nothing is flipped, and nothing is raised.

**What I got wrong.** P14b predicted that the switch's money would move through `parity`, stayers put onto fixes, positive on at least 3 of 4 seeds with a mean of +£1,500. It was positive on 2 of 4, with a mean of +£309. Seed 5 read −£2,085, and one household (`SYN-2016-145`, a 2019 fix it declined under flat) carried −£5,293 of that. Why that fix cost so much is not traced. Parity is the noisiest channel, not the one the money moves through.

**Stated beside the grade.** Flat and the offer arms also differ in collections tone. The tone reaches no payment, since one payment truth (`ded298ecd2`, an ancestor of the arms' commit), as §17 found (`1044c8fe0`). So the comparison is the offers alone. That rests on the code path. It was not re-measured on these arms.

**Next.** A new rule asking more seeds of the ending-term arm would be a new pre-registration. It is not worth its compute until a grader splits net per household, because gross overstates what one departure costs by 2 to 3.6 times on seeds 1 to 4.

## 2026-10-23 — Each of the eight layers on How it's built carries its own evidence, counted at publish from the store that records it; proven able to fail is now counted over the tests

<!-- head: d5cd1359dbf7 -->

**In plain English:** Each of the eight layers of checks on How it's built now shows its own evidence, counted at publish: how often it fired in the last 30 days, when it last fired, and whether a test has been seen to fail on its defect.

*Seat executor, 23 Oct 2026. Director, 23 Oct 09:20 (advisor channel, DIRECTOR_STEER_SHOW_THE_HARNESS_AS_A_LIVE_CONTROL_STACK): "How could you show our harness and e2e control mechanism, is very advanced".*

**What each box counts, and why the units differ.** Each layer reads the one store that already records it, and its box names that unit. (1) Commits carrying the `Director-doc:` reason the director-document gate demands. (2) Sourced research documents added, each of which the knowledge gate reads. (3) Tool calls the lane hook denied; the network wall refuses by construction and leaves nothing to count. (4) Commit attempts that the publisher logged as refused; no other agent logs its gate, and the box says so. (5) Test files that record a mutation. (6) Blind reviews recorded in their ledger. (7) Publish-gate runs that stopped a publish. (8) Mistake classes registered. "Shown able to fail" counts the tests that both name the layer's own files and record a mutation. A store that is not on the machine gives "not measured yet", never a 0.

**At d5cd1359d, read against the shared tree's stores:**
- Director documents: 40 marked commits.
- Research documents: 61 added.
- Wall denials: 0, last on 4 Sep.
- Publisher commit attempts: 14 of 35 refused.
- Tests proven able to fail: 532 of 2,154.
- Blind reviews: 10.
- Publish-gate runs: 28 of 81 stopped a publish.
- Mistake classes: 0 new, last on 28 Aug.

The two rare layers, 3 and 8, show their numbers plainly, as the steer asks.

**Layer 5 is defined over the tests now, not over the July register** (the finding was moved to done). The scale strip's "33 of 35 registered controls" became "532 tests proven able to fail", and the register's figure sits beside it. A test counts when a docstring or other string in it records a MUTATION, read through `ast.parse`. - invert the refused outcome (it survived at first because the fixture held one pass and one refusal; a second pass row was added);
- drop the MUTATION marker;

- read the raw text, not the code, for which module a test names.

   household?", one sentence on what it is, then M1 and M11 verbatim.

   from research notes, counted from git at publish), then the run strip (168,026 half hours, the

   `site/test_the_front_doors_capability_grid_names_a_test_for_every_line.py`: it reds when a line
   names no test, or a test that no longer exists. A live mutation (a renamed test path) went red.

     credit assessment, switch governance with its 14-day cooling-off, change of supplier)
   - Pricing under the cap -> knowledge/price-cap (an SVT segment held at the published cap; renewal desk)

   - Half-hourly settlement -> knowledge/imbalance-cashout-settlement (settlement; hedged settlement)

     opening DD is never the first issued bill)
   - Collections and debt, IFRS 9 -> knowledge/debt-and-collections (collections journey; cash
     forecast provision; closed-balance write-off)
   - Back-billing and read duties, SLC 21BA and 21B.4 -> knowledge/back-billing-and-liability
   - Capital adequacy -> capabilities/#supplier (capital adequacy tests)
   - Household carbon per half hour -> explore/#used (half-hourly footprint; the gas leg)

   changes and moves, and the wall. The segment check's `data-mix-claim` now sits here. The model
   on one page follows, unchanged except for one corrected sentence (below).
5. Built and run by AI: the build loop, the checks that must be able to fail, a link to the code
   graph, and the dual-fuel episode.
6. The open question, in one line, carrying `data-selection-verdict` and `data-selection-draws`,
   so the publish gates still hold it to `value_arms.json`. Then "What is not built yet ->" and
   "What we know is wrong ->", and three doors.

## 2026-10-22 — The banner's false episode closed at the producer, a frozen 'Right now' count on How it's built, and a profiled home now settles on its profile

<!-- head: ed071724658c -->

*Autonomous worker, 22 Oct 2026, evening. Drawn: the lane-0 item a-profiled-home-settles-its-own-volume-on-its-registered-profile. The director's banner steer came first, under the advisor-channel rung.*

## The banner: what was false, and the producer side

The front door's "PUBLISHING IS FAILING ... over 80.0h" was not the browser reading a frozen site copy, which is what the advisor took it for. The liveness-branch heartbeat was current (13:40Z today). It carried the publisher's own record, and that record still held an open episode. Monday's publish `2a195224b` was merged onto origin by a seat (`f8f3d0fd5`), not pushed by the publisher, so `record_publish_gate_success` never ran. The episode's cause (`gate_refusal`) is not one git can re-ask, so `close_episode_if_cause_cleared` logged "only a publish can close this episode" eleven times while a publish already had.

Two lanes fixed it from opposite ends, independently and within 20 minutes. `8bf9103a1` (the seat executor) makes the reader, `publisher_refusal`, read `held` once a publish has landed inside the episode. That lane also took the banner off the home page, put the quiet "Figures from the run of 19 Oct 2026 · published every Monday" line in its place, and showed that today's four red deploys all deployed, with only the served-bytes window failing. `383adfab9` (this tick) makes the producer close the episode when git's date for the figures on origin is later than `wedge_since` (rule `publish_landed`). I then ran that close once on the live record: it now reads `held`, next publish Mon 26 Oct 04:00, closed by `publish_landed`. The two fixes complement each other. The reader's fix stops the false word, and the producer's fix stops the false episode.

## The class sweep (steer item 2), by count

Six `site/data/*.json` files carry runtime state and are rendered on a page. Three age themselves against the reader's clock: `tick_heartbeat.json`, `publish_provenance.json` and `delivery.json`. Three did not:
- `director_reserved.json` (How it's built): **"Right now nothing is waiting on him", from a file last written on 18 Sep.** Fixed in the commit carrying this entry. The page now says "Right now" only while the count is under 8 days old (one weekly cadence plus a day). Past that it names the day it was counted and says the count is too old to say what is waiting now. Mutation-proven. **Owed:** the producer. Nothing has refreshed the file since 19 Sep.
- `proof.json` `renderStamp` and `director_delta.json`: they show their own dates as labels but do not gate on them. Both refresh with each weekly publish, so they are inside the bound today. A shared self-age check across the site is still owed.

## The settlement build (the drawn item)

A fabric home without HH settlement is now billed on its meter and bought on its registered profile, trued up to its own volume over each term. That is how a 2016–2025 domestic meter was settled. The prereg (P15) was written before the code, and the full book was graded through the run's own writer. P15a is exact: 2,472 home-years, max gap £0.0000, no revenue moved. P15b holds: night-heavy electric +£16.9 a year, day-heated electric −£37.3, gas-heated +£1.5. The book barely moves (+£3,030 gross), because the two electric groups mostly cancel. The PC3 SMEs' +£100 a year does not move, because their shape is already their profile. The +£100 is the weather adjustment against the raw 1997 table, a GAP. The run-level grade after hedging waits for a published run. The front door's garbled settlement sentence (steer item 4) is rewritten with the measured figure, in the same commit.

## What I got wrong

P15c's arithmetic summed the two electric subgroups and missed the one home between them: £3,043 predicted against £3,030 measured. It is kept beside the result.

## Still owed from the steer

The producer for `director_reserved.json`; the site-wide self-age check; publisher state as an operational line on How it's built; item 5, the Claude Code package. The mover work is already drawn in DIRECTION.yaml.

<!-- head: 4d9442253627 -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-22T11:21:39.215744+00:00; 13 commits, 6 substantive, since 2026-10-22T08:24:35.466585+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 0 world, 1 both, 11 other.

## What the stretch meant

Forward on inference, sideways on levels: no level moved. There were 13 commits, 11 carrying work and 6 substantive. The brief's split reads supplier 1, both 1, other 11, because it sorts by file. Read by subject, seven of the eleven are grades and pre-registrations of supplier experiments, three are the director's front-door steer, and one is D48 billing (c6c09641e). No world build landed. THE STEER: two of four focus items were drawn and landed: the lower-bound retention guard (766d26fc6) and the HEAD run with its grades (4eb192b60). The bill estimator and the meter-exchange prereg were not drawn. Lane 0 works in order, and the first two items filled the stretch. Both are carried, and the estimator now goes first, because billing accuracy is first in his order and got one commit this stretch. WHAT IT MEANS. (1) The company learned something from its own data, and the thing it learned is that its lever does nothing. Section 15's holdout (4d82dce3b): the holdout lost 8 of 21 and the offered group 26 of 62, so the learned save rate is 0, where section 13's belief ratio read 0.19. changed_a_departure is 0 in both arms. On this book, retention offers are transfer, not creation (M2). That is the thesis working as designed, inference refusing a lever, but it removes one place the per-customer company could beat flat. The lower-bound guard now refuses to offer while the interval includes zero (-0.089 [-0.986, +0.403]). It is raised for the director because, from a cold start, it can never learn. Section 16 launched at 11:24Z (4d94422536). (2) Per-customer against flat has its first valid seed. Seed 2 holds P14a'. After the grader fix (9fc114520), ending_term minus flat parity reads +GBP 2,866, not the -GBP 25 first graded. The one save (+GBP 5,190) is a household the save-odds guard made no offer to. One seed of four is not a comparison. Seed 3 is running. (3) The BLOCKING crisis finding moved, and it is still open. On the HEAD run 989ce4f1c2 (unpublished), the IFRS 9 crisis share is 0.70%, inside the 0.50-0.80% prediction, but the step-up is x0.96, against a predicted x1.1-1.5. The pre-crisis 2016-19 charge rose x3.3, and the crisis charge lands almost all in 2023, a year after the real step. Whether that is the world's arrears or the matrix's ageing, I cannot yet say. Item 2 reads it. It is not an attribution run, because three world changes moved together. (4) Billing: post-departure gas billing falls from 147 bills (GBP 4,715.70) to none on the HEAD run. Gas prepayment read instructions now follow UNC M5.9.14. D48's held bills are 9, as before. The catch-up driver (the three-read re-level) is untouched. Corrected this stretch: the seat's save-rate instruction is now refuted on the run and superseded, and the section 14 grader's parity edge is fixed (both in wrong).

## 2026-10-22 — The front door steer, done: two cold readers both took it for a real company, and what the page now says because of them

<!-- head: 53ff7189b9d0 -->

The director's front-door steer of 22 Oct ("Do it", 07:29 BST) is done, apart from two points that wait on him or on research, listed at the end. Five landings: 5765c102d (item 1), 420a5b67d (items 2, 3, 4, 7, 8), 2259b7b39 (items 5, 6), 0caf19169 (item 9, the canon-against-site check and the proof-strip label), and the cold-reader fixes landed with this entry.

**Each stale claim, before and after** (item 1, in full in the steer's Progress section):
- Headline. "An energy company built and run by AI, to find the cheapest tonne of carbon left" became what it is in two lines, then M1 verbatim, then M11. After the cold read it begins "A simulated GB energy supplier".
- Whose book this is. "As of 24 August … more than 98% of the revenue" became households, mostly dual fuel, with the I&C suspension told as history.
- Time. "Time does not appear in this project at all" became "Time is defined but not yet measured" (M3).
- The world. "Every property is one national shape rescaled" became the per-building thermal model where the weather store covers a home, and the national shape elsewhere.
- Carbon. "The carbon meter is designed but not yet wired" became: household emissions are measured, abatement is not (CO4).
- Knowledge. The dead "results live on Proof" became Capabilities and Explore.
- Explore's "a supplier with this few accounts" was checked and still holds.

**The front door now reads:** what it is (two lines), M1, M11, the proof strip, "what it has found", two ways in (energy, tech), whose book this is, then the claim. The long caveats sit one click down, each under a one-line pointer. None was deleted.

**Proof strip sources.** All three figures are written into the HTML at publish by `generate_dashboard_data.write_front_door_proof_strip`, none typed:
- half-hourly periods: `site/data/sim_data.json` metadata (Elexon system prices);
- the years: the run's annual accounts;
- households: the run's final-year book, counted per household, not per fuel account.

"Days since a human wrote code" is left out, because git authorship cannot tell a human from a machine here. "Tests and commits" is left out because RC5 bans effort metrics on the front door, and that conflict is in `for_the_director`. The cold reader read "10 calendar years" as ten whole years, but the record ends 7 Jun 2025. The label now says so (0caf19169) and changes at Monday's publish.

**Stories, and why each was chosen:**
- The 17–19 Oct dual-fuel episode: a real defect against a published 72%, found by his question and fixed with checks inside a day.
- The three-arm value test: "we cannot tell yet", the canon's own credible result.
- Half-hourly carbon timing: a real measured difference, honestly scoped.

**Vocabulary** (2259b7b39):
- "wall" became "what the company can see";
- "seams, where the curtain is" became "where the simulation would meet the real industry";
- "rungs" became "sources", and "atoms" became "build-plan items";
- Harness became "How it's built", same URL, second in the nav.

The machinery page keeps its terms, with each one defined once. After the cold read, three more internal names left the front door: "SETTLEMENT_CEILING_2026-08-24", "director-canon, v4" and "no glossary needed".

**No-JS render.** The strip and headline figures are in the published bytes. `site/test_home_door.py` reds if a script fills them again.

**Deploy exclusion and its check** (0caf19169):
- `--stage` leaves out the 65 test and helper `.py` files and the five `_*.mjs` harnesses, then reads the staged tree back and fails if one got through.
- The post-deploy check no longer waits on them.
- No page links any of them.
- The GitHub Pages manifest publishes `docs/` only, and a test keeps scripts out of it.
- Copies already at the edge may linger in Pages' cache. A deploy cannot prove those gone.

**Canon against site.** `canon_drift_check` now reads all 41 served pages as visible text against 147 canon quotes and the §16 superseded framings. All hold. M1 is the one quote a page starts, and the front door carries it verbatim. Text written by a page's JavaScript is not read here; that is the door tests' job. Four mutations each went red.

**Cold-reader answers.** Two fresh readers had only the front door's visible text: an energy professional and a technologist.
- *What is this?* Both got it right in the end, and both first read it as a real company: the hero said "supplier" and "No customers" came a paragraph later. Fixed: "A simulated…". The technologist could not tell whether a language model makes the decisions at run time. Fixed: one sentence says the code the AI wrote decides, and that code cannot reach the internet.
- *What has it shown?* Both found the three-arm test the one strong design, with a null result. Both called the dual-fuel story a bug report, which is honest but not a result. The energy reader called half-hourly carbon trivial to anyone who has used the carbon-intensity API.
- *Why believe it?* Both trusted the publish stamps and "we cannot tell yet". The energy reader's sharpest line: "hides nothing" above a page with no margin, bad debt or £ saved. Those figures are kept off the front door on purpose (RC7: no cohort £ there) and live on Capabilities and Explore. The technologist found M11 asserted, not substantiated, and asked for a repository link. That waits on him: the repository is public, but a July plan meant to make it private. Raised in `for_the_director` with a recommendation to link it.
- Also fixed: "a fixed set of founder households" beside "a fresh mix every run" (founders are drawn per seed); the two meanings of "saved" (against the default tariff, against simpler rules) are now told apart.

**Not fixed, and why:**
- The energy reader said domestic supply was mostly profile-settled in that decade, so "each household's metered half hours" overstates the data a 2018 supplier had.
- The same reader said Triads ended in April 2023. That is only partly right as I understand TCR, and it is unverified.
- The 2014 CMA survey behind the dual-fuel story has newer Ofgem figures.
- The £273/tCO₂e needs its price base year.

Each of these needs published evidence before the page changes (K1, K4), so they are handed on as one research item, not guessed at here.

## What the stretch meant

The retention lever is now known to be nearly inert at the roll, and the money per-customer retention made against flat is transfer and noise. 10 commits, 8 carrying work, 5 substantive. The brief's split (0 supplier, 2 world, 1 both, 7 other) is by file. Read by subject, it is even: the holdout (fdec35bd9) and the section 14 seed grader (bc1e6ad78) are supplier. The dual-leaver fix (2b81e1466) is a billing-accuracy defect in the world, which is first in his order. The held-money flip (6b81d3b25) is what the BLOCKING crisis bad-debt finding waits on. The roll-offer trace (f3dae1d50) is a read of the world. All four items in the last focus were drawn and three landed. The fourth, D48's practice-or-defect table, was spent before I filed it: e885e30ff and f2db4aa45 had already graded PROS-2017-0336's catch-up as two held months, the screen doing what section 4d intends. D48 is also not a BUILD-stage atom, so the draw cannot classify it, and an atom-id focus item cannot reach it. That is the seat's error, listed in wrong. No level moved. WHAT IT MEANS. (1) The lever: a roll offer does reach the leaving household's choice, with no ordering defect. It is too small to move it. A 3% median discount lifts P(stay) by 0.77 points, which is one save in 101 offers (f3dae1d50). On the default dice, section 12's +GBP 111 against flat is one extra departure (-GBP 2,035) against seven stayers moved onto fixes (+GBP 2,308) (bc1e6ad78). So on this world the per-customer company's retention money is M2 transfer plus one coin. The thesis survives only if the company can LEARN that from what it holds and then stops paying stayers. The holdout is how a real supplier learns it. It is built, default off, and its arm is running (s15). But at 27% of about 83 offers a year it resolves the break-even difference, not a 1% save rate. So the next supplier question is what the guard does while its save rate cannot be told from zero (item 3). (2) Inference: the ending-term belief still ranks leavers at 0.806 in the run. Section 14's four dice seeds are running, and no policy carries the belief yet. The s1 and s15 arms were launched before 2b81e1466, so their levels still carry that gas. Their paired differences stand. (4) The BLOCKING crisis finding: both world switches it waited on are now default on (shortfall on the month's demand; held money as a part payment). ## 2026-10-22 — orientation: The per-customer view now aims, and the lever it aims does not work

<!-- head: 7939895894fe -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-22T02:22:49.530184+00:00; 19 commits, 7 substantive, since 2026-10-21T23:20:03.399436+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 3 world, 1 both, 14 other.

## What the stretch meant

The per-customer view now aims, and the lever it aims does not work. 19 commits, 16 carrying work, 7 substantive. The brief's split (1 supplier, 3 world, 1 both, 14 other) is by file. Of the 14 'other', the section 12 and 13 grades are supplier and five are world grades or records, so the world still had more commits than the supplier. That is defensible only because those world builds (the shortfall shared on the month's demand, now default on at 5c0eeeb48; money held toward a bill as a part payment, seed 1 graded) are what the BLOCKING crisis bad-debt finding waits on. All three items in the last focus were drawn. Two landed: the retention guard weighing its save odds (0674199b8, graded 67186eb59) and the bad-debt belief read by vintage (793989589). D48's practice-or-defect table did not land. No level moved. WHAT IT MEANS. (1) Inference: with the shrinkage prior, the ending-term belief keeps its aim in the run (AUC 0.806 [0.745, 0.860], a7fc5c728) and the 2017 fix-end multiplier reads 1.215, not 3.39. So the K2 defect is gone and the company now ranks leavers using only what it holds. (2) Lever: at the roll it priced, a retention offer kept nobody: 0 of 37 in section 7, and 0 of the 32 offers section 13 withdrew. The company's save rate read 0.19 all the same, because it is 1 minus observed over expected on offered accounts. That measures the belief's calibration on the offered tail, and the code's own docstring says only a holdout separates the two. (3) Money: section 12's +GBP 810 over section 13 came from five stayers whom the discount moved onto a fix that later cost them more than the default. Under M2 that is transfer, not creation. So on this seed the only money per-customer retention made against flat was taken from households who were staying anyway. That is backwards against the thesis, and it is the most important thing this stretch found. Against flat the result is a tie (+GBP 111 for section 12, -GBP 699 for section 13), on one seed. (4) Billing accuracy: 187c2a999 found that a dual household which leaves on its electricity leg goes on being billed gas for 82 to 345 days. It bisects to c136809f53, the commit that made the book 73.6% dual. Every arm since then bills energy to households that have gone and books debt on accounts nobody holds, so it comes first. (5) The bad-debt belief can no longer go negative. It is fixed as a class at both doors (793989589), and its before/after table on the net arm is running (probe r2; the first probe died on an import path). (6) The 'director inputs' in this brief are not his. They are a peer session's cross-session messages, recorded as his console. They are listed in wrong and treated as data.

## 2026-10-22 — orientation: The supplier's per-customer view now ranks leavers better than chance, and it does so in the run

<!-- head: df9792c5736e -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-21T23:20:03.399436+00:00; 21 commits, 7 substantive, since 2026-10-21T20:20:12.217037+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 0 world, 1 both, 19 other.

## What the stretch meant

The supplier's per-customer view now ranks leavers better than chance, and it does so in the run. That is the thesis's inference, measured for the first time. It has not yet turned into money against flat. 21 commits, 19 carrying work, 7 substantive. The brief's split (1 supplier, 1 both, 19 other) is by file. Twelve of the 'other' are grades and censuses filed as staging records: five supplier, seven world. All four items in the last focus were drawn and landed (7a7ad95dc, e885e30ff, c95f28d8a, 983ff2e22), and so were their continuations. No level moved. WHAT IT MEANS. (1) The renewal churn belief, conditioned on the term now ending (7a7ad95dc, default off), ranks leavers at AUC 0.819 [0.757, 0.877] out of sample from 2019, where the current belief reads 0.333. It uses only a field the company already held. In the run (f16695c2a) the aim carries through: in-run AUC 0.819, and default-term states lower on 216 of 222. But the design had no prior, so two closed 2016 fix-ends set a multiplier of 3.39 for 2017. Offers rose from 113 to 134 and cost rose by GBP 544. The +GBP 1,125 against flat is five households trading places on one seed, so it is not attributable. e856ddc69 shrinks the multiplier by a width the record gives (Ofgem EFTC against CMOC, prior variance 0.28 in log space), and section 12's rerun is live and claimed. So the inference is real. Whether it creates value still needs seeds, and the EP17 seed listing is the director's open row. (2) The F11 check came out in our favour. Blind to company results, 983ff2e22 puts the world's default-tariff drift (0.107 a year realised) and its no-roll-at-anniversary rule inside both published bands. So the roll-type gain is not the world flattering the company. (3) Retention netting does nothing to debtors (df9792c57: 6 offers withdrawn, none from a debtor, +GBP 29). It surfaced one real company defect: default_belief goes negative on thin cells. That is focus item 2. (4) Billing: the catch-up premise was wrong. The fields were already on the published row (e885e30ff). 371 catch-ups reach back more than 12 months and 168 of them are undercharges. None breaches SLC 21BA: the pay-on-bill ones are capped or predate May 2018, and the direct-debit ones are barred at the recovery action. D48 held 9 bills, none for more than three months. D48 L3 now waits only on the world's smart-meter exchange flip, and its four-arm trigger is met with df9792c57. (5) The BLOCKING crisis bad-debt finding narrowed to one world rule. Indebted leavers are not selection: their fall is the switching freeze, sized like the record (c95f28d8a). Arrears sit about two bills deep, x4-6 short of Ofgem's series, because ENERGY_SHARES_THE_SHORTFALL shares money pro rata with the debt stock. That fixes depth at C/(A-B), a median of 1.67 bills (3e52f2baf, predicted 1-3). The stock-versus-demand one-variable pair is running, claimed as W2_shortfall_shared_on_demand, so it is not in focus: a second claim would be a second writer. The publisher has been FAILING for 62h and is held to 26 Oct. Nothing went backwards. The money comparison against flat stands where it stood: tied on one seed, waiting on seeds.

## 2026-10-21 — orientation: Per-customer inference against the flat baseline now has a measured cause: the inference fails, not the lever alone

<!-- head: 782f50df98e5 -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-21T20:20:12.217037+00:00; 13 commits, 2 substantive, since 2026-10-21T17:24:18.309623+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 0 world, 0 both, 12 other.

## What the stretch meant

Per-customer inference against the flat baseline now has a measured cause: the inference fails, not the lever alone. 13 commits, 10 carrying work, 2 substantive. The brief's split is 1 supplier, 0 world, 12 other, but that split is by file: seven of the 'other' are supplier grades filed as staging records. Both items in the last focus were drawn and landed (7dc923787, 5336ddb20), and so were all four continuations. No level moved. WHAT IT MEANS. (1) The flat-arm tie is split (7dc923787, 76a29bd92, 7eb9f2695). The company's renewal churn belief ranks the flat arm's 110 switch leavers at AUC 0.46 [0.40, 0.52], and from 2019 at 0.33, which is worse than chance. The world's own probability ranks the same leavers at 0.90. The retention offers reached 44 would-be leavers and kept 4. The cause is that the belief is higher on the rolls that rarely lose anyone. The world rolls departure dice at the end of a fix (40 of 92 leave from 2019), not at an SVT conversion or a declined fix (6 of 176). The company holds the tariff type and does not use it. Roll type alone ranks at 0.818, and roll type plus price position, fitted before 2019, at 0.742. This is a modelling gap the company can close from what it already knows, which is the thesis's inference, not access. Item 1 builds it. Two cautions go with it. Inside end-of-fix rolls even the world's own probability reads only 0.65, so the gain is in when to act, not whom to pick. And whether the world is right to put no departure risk on a default-tariff roll is a world question. Item 4 answers it from published evidence, blind to this grade, because a gain built on a world rule too sharp to be real would be the world flattering us (F11). (2) The opex credit is graded (e9e2fbe71): the median renewal is +GBP 2.29 a month, not -3.91. C34 still advises 4 of 975 rows, so the C34 concern's recommendation stands, with its evidence corrected. (3) E6's D1 fix (aef898e0e) makes the early warning honest and about neutral, so it stays off. (4) Bad debt is now traced, not just attributed (782f50df9). The live receivable matches between world and company to the penny. Closed-account debt is held or written off at 365 days. The crisis adds almost no new leaver debt (GBP 100 in 2022, 324 in 2023, against about 1k a year in 2017-18). The BLOCKING finding's open side is therefore the world's indebted-leaver flow, and item 3 is the census that says whether that is selection or a world rule. (5) Billing: D48's held estimates fell to 9 on 4 accounts. Its catch-up bound cannot be read because the published bills drop the catchup_* fields, and one listed dwelling went 14 months without a bill before a GBP 5,067 catch-up. That is a back-billing question, and item 2 makes it gradable. The publisher has been FAILING for 59h and is held to 26 Oct. The retnet pair is running (off arm since 18:26Z). Its driver files the grade.

## What the stretch meant

Level on code, and the first reading of the thesis comparison itself is a tie. 12 commits, all carrying work, 6 substantive; the brief splits them 1 supplier, 0 world, 11 other, but that split is by file, and most of the 11 are supplier grades filed as staging records. All three of last record's items were drawn and landed: the D48 instrument (8e99f83cd), E6's early-warning slice (cda47a346) and the brief's draw-hold reasons (b0963f254). No level moved. WHAT IT MEANS. (1) The per-customer switches against flat rules, one seed, one book (c576f5f98): flat has one fewer departure and is GBP 97 ahead. Targeted retention moved about GBP 2.8k to households to keep about two. The renewal desk advises in 39% of decision states, but 508 of 514 advised rows carry C35's rise, so advice without a rise is 0.44%. On this evidence the per-customer supplier does not yet beat the baseline, and nobody yet knows whether the cause is inference (the belief cannot find the leavers) or the lever (it finds them and the offer moves nothing). The one-variable fix is landing now (surgical_land pid 50155) under its continuation, so it is not in focus. (3) Bad debt is attributed but not solved. The budget switches raise the IFRS 9 crisis share from 0.14% to 0.40% (a8e06397c). The finding stays BLOCKING because 0.40% is still 2.5x under the 1% floor, and nobody has said whether that gap is the world's arrears volume or the company's provision rate. Item 2 decides which side it belongs to. (4) The queue: the scopex credit arm finished at 16:54Z and nocredit is running (the import death was fixed by 693353e7e), so the -GBP 3.91 grade is near 18:30Z. ## 2026-10-21 — orientation: Level, not backwards

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-21T11:22:31.343264+00:00; 9 commits, 5 substantive, since 2026-10-21T08:22:59.835213+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 1 world, 0 both, 7 other.

## What the stretch meant

Level, not backwards. The machine got safer, and the thesis comparison is half run and not yet graded. 9 commits, all carrying work, 5 substantive. The brief splits them 1 supplier, 1 world, 7 other; read by subject, the supplier share is larger, because two of the 'other' commits are D48's and the retention-netting prereg's. No level moved. Every one of the previous focus's five items was drawn, and four finished. The per-customer worktree is locked (1ac35d918). The meter exchange landed behind a switch that is off (a60376f88). The retention-netting prereg landed (c0b75a932), and its arm pair has a live driver. A queued long job now waits in a unit of its own (26a030c8f), which corrects the vanished-arms row. D48 was drawn and built nothing (0f8048366), correctly, because its L3 waits on a run and not on code. WHAT IT MEANS. (1) The test of the thesis is running, not graded. The current arm finished in 2h26m (rc 0), all_on is 1h34m in, and flat follows, so the grade lands near 14:40Z. Its continuation is embargoed to exactly then, which is why item 3 makes it wait for flat.rc. That book is a diagnostic only; the real grade still needs the director's six EP17 seeds. (2) Compute, not code, is now the supplier's bottleneck. Four arm sets queue one after another until about 01:00Z tomorrow: per-customer, scopex (the opex credit that decides whether the -GBP 3.91 renewal figure is real), baddebt (the BLOCKING crisis bad-debt control), and retention netting. The sim-runner defers to all of them, so D48's held-bill run cannot happen today. Item 1 makes the netting pair's off arm that run, for free. Item 2 is supplier work that needs no compute: E6's early warning, landed off. (3) The seat's own error this stretch: it ordered D48's Expert Hour before the review's inputs existed. That is recorded and corrected. The publisher has said FAILING for 50h, and the publish is held to 26 Oct.

## 2026-10-21 — 2026-10-21 — founder households: first production peak at the new shape is 5,115.6 MB, under the 5,708 trigger (1 of 3)

<!-- head: 9e273a69e32a -->

Step 3 of the 20 Oct founder-households ruling (his caveat: watch the first three production peaks at the new shape against 6,008 MB). One of three has closed.

| # | Run (git) | Carries 8927e9345 | Shape at that git | Process peak | Cgroup memory peak | Wall time | Reaper |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9ca972774, started 03:54:33 BST, closed 06:25:50 | yes (`merge-base --is-ancestor`) | founder_unit: households, 400; budget 7,700.0 | **5,115.6 MB** | 6.3G | 9,077 s | did not fire (no kill/OOM line in the journal) |

Against the allowance: 5,115.6 MB is 892.4 MB under 6,008 MB and 592.4 MB under the 5,708 MB trigger (within 5%). The trigger is not met, so production stays at 7,700 and no fallback commit is made. It is 224 MB below the probe's 5,340 MB and 1,075.8 MB above the last old-book run (ec7fd9942, 4,039.8 MB). The held draw run time was 9,232 s, and this run took 9,077 s.

Which peak counts. The cgroup peak (6.3G) is not the run's measure. Since 38f3a565f the trace build's forked workers fill whatever memory is free, so the cgroup peak measures the box (background/sim_runner.py, the comment on the process-peak line). The process peak is ru_maxrss over reaped children, which is what the ceiling's curve prices. The old-book run's cgroup peak was 5.8G, against a 4,039.8 MB process peak.

Control. tests/simulation/test_net_new_acquisition.py::test_the_ceiling_still_fits_the_peak_systemds_own_journal_reports_today ran at 06:46 BST and PASSED. It was armed, not skipped: the only run in its window that carries the shape commits is this one.

Still open: runs 2 and 3. Handed off under a new id. The runner is in its between-run pause: it was holding 3,571 s at 06:44 BST. The next run should therefore start around 07:44 and close around 10:15, and a third around 14:15 if the cadence holds.

## 2026-10-21 — Founder households, step 3: no run at the new shape has closed yet, and the ceiling's journal leg was passing on the old book's peak

<!-- head: 551b025aba6f -->

Step 3 of the 400-household ruling (`docs/staging/advisor/done/DIRECTOR_RULING_FOUNDER_HOUSEHOLDS_WITH_BUDGET_RAISED_2026-10-20.md`)
asks for the peak of each of the first three production runs at the new shape, against 6,008 MB.
**Read at 04:35 BST on 21 Oct: none has closed.**

| sim-runner lifetime | code | carries 8927e9345 | process peak | systemd memory peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 Oct 21:44 to 21 Oct 00:14 | ec7fd9942 | **no** (old shape: 400 supply points, budget 5,000) | 4,039.8 MB | 5.8G |
| 00:14 to 02:14 | none ran | n/a | n/a | 13.5M (deferred) |
| 02:14 to 03:44 | none ran | n/a | n/a | 14M (deferred) |
| started 03:54 | 9ca972774 | yes | running | running |

The runner was deferred from 00:41 to 03:49 by long-job admission. The admitted job was
`longjob-read-instruction-ceiling-8927e9345`, declared at 7,000 MB, which ran for 130 minutes against its
declared 120. That job ran on the new code. systemd reports a 6.1G cgroup peak for it, but it is an
experiment arm, not a sim-runner run, and a cgroup peak is not the process figure the 6,008 allowance
is set against. The pre-switch run shows the gap: 5.8G cgroup against 4,039.8 MB process. So it is
recorded here and is not one of the three. No reaper fired and the rule did not trip. The founder
unit and budget stay as they are.

**The ceiling's journal leg was green for the wrong reason, and is fixed.**
`test_the_ceiling_still_fits_the_peak_systemds_own_journal_reports_today` counted a peak when its
run carried the curve's `git_head`. That head is 7858b89a6, the commit the probe worktree sat on with the
400-household shape still uncommitted, and it is older than 8927e9345, which landed the shape.
So ec7fd9942's 4,039.8 MB peak from the lighter old book re-priced the ceiling for 7,700 and passed. A
peak now counts only when its run also carries the last commit that set `founder_unit`/`founder_accounts`
and the last commit that set the budget. Against the same journal the leg now skips as UNAVAILABLE.
The mutation, keying on the curve head alone, passed on this same journal before the fix.
The 03:54 run carries all three commits, so the leg arms when that run closes.

Hand-off: `founder-households-first-three-peaks-2`, to read the 03:54 run and the next two.

## 2026-10-21 — orientation: Forward on billing and on the instruments, not yet on the thesis

<!-- head: 2da5d3ee740f -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-21T02:20:57.325479+00:00; 5 commits, 2 substantive, since 2026-10-20T23:24:15.597403+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 0 world, 0 both, 4 other.

## What the stretch meant

Forward on billing and on the instruments, not yet on the thesis. 5 commits, 2 substantive, 0 that carried no work. The brief splits them 1 supplier, 0 world, 4 other. Read by subject, all five were supplier work: D48's closed-account estimate (7a266cb76) and its page (2da5d3ee7), the read instruction's arms tool (1a40d8b99), and the opex-credit grading fix (193ae19be). No level moved. What it MEANS. (1) Billing, first in his order: a held estimate on a closed account now goes out on its final bill at the closing read (7a266cb76). The last D48 hold, four actual-read bills at founder C8's home, is in surgical_land now (pid 644310). D48 failed its L3 Expert Hour on 14 Oct because the accrual its title claims was not built. That accrual is now built and graded (75aff1401, d4af471a1), so the reason for the failure may be gone. Nobody has re-asked, which is focus item 3. (2) The licence duty is being measured. All three read-instruction arms are running at 8927e9345 (2h35m in, about 11 GB), and their grade is queued for 04:45. So last stretch's item 1 was drawn, handed on and leaves focus. (3) The comparison the thesis is judged on has still not run. Every per-customer decision has a production caller behind an off switch, the standing-charge credit is in the code (ec7fd9942), and the honest within-segment test still reads 'cannot tell' in two of three years. The previous focus named 3 items and 1 was drawn. The other two (the book-size question and the three-arm run) were not drawn. That is not yet drift, because the stretch lasted 2.9h and the one executor slot was spent on item 1 and D48. They stay as items 1 and 2, with the cheap read-only measurement first, because it decides whether the director's six EP17 seeds can answer at all. (4) The opex credit's grade did not run. Its arms were held behind a landing and never started (193ae19be), so the C34 concern's premise stays unre-read for another stretch. The box is now the constraint: the read arms hold about 11 GB, the credit arms are queued behind them, and the three-arm run will queue behind both. (5) The machine. The launch-reading miss I had called unexplained recurred, and the brief's own code explains it. The 'none launched or ended' sentence reads only ENDED jobs, while three launches sit in the register inside this stretch. That is a one-line instrument fix, focus item 4. The publisher has reported FAILING for 41h, against a publish held to 26 Oct.

## 2026-10-21 — orientation: Forward, and the supplier's half of the comparison is now built end to end, but the thesis still reads 'cannot tell'

<!-- head: 8927e9345ce3 -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-20T23:24:15.597403+00:00; 17 commits, 8 substantive, since 2026-10-20T17:23:16.844326+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 3 world, 3 both, 10 other.

## What the stretch meant

Forward, and the supplier's half of the comparison is now built end to end, but the thesis still reads 'cannot tell'. 17 commits, 8 substantive (4 carried no work, all merges). The brief splits them 1 supplier, 3 world, 3 both, 10 other. Read by subject the stretch was mostly supplier: of the three 'world' commits, 066fd2300 served D48, and 768f41ed1 (the budget decides payment by default) and 8927e9345 (400 founder households and a settlement budget of 7,700) carried out the director's rulings. No level moved. What it MEANS. (1) Every per-customer decision now has a production caller: C34 (18503313a), the save offer (46387b883) and C35 (466fb691e, merged 14df12a5f). All sit behind switches that default off, so the standing company is still a flat-rules player. They have never run switched on together against the flat supplier on one book. That run is focus item 3. (2) The baseline's retention control can now fail. abe7ce533 keys it to the cut over 2017, and a flat arm that offers reds all three flat legs. The control was not made blind by c61d8b608, as my last record said. 2016 held 3 renewals, all below the churn threshold, so it had always read 0 against 0. (3) The median renewal's -GBP 3.91 a month was OURS, not the world's. The term contribution charged the operating cost the standing charge recovers and credited none of it (f04bd6102). ec7fd9942 credits it, and its grade is queued for 02:00. So the C34 concern's premise ('our side negative in almost every renewal') was partly an allocation of ours. I will re-read that concern's evidence once the grade lands. (4) Billing, first in his order: the company now computes its unbilled accrual and no longer counts a bill its pre-bill gate held as billed (75aff1401, d4af471a1). The council tax lookup now asks about the dwelling (066fd2300). What is left of the accrual is held bills that nothing ever works, and two continuations carry it. Against the thesis itself: B11's within-segment term (27ca9dc7a, last stretch) is the honest test of inference against the flat rule. It clears only in 2020, by a hair (+0.061, interval +0.002 to +0.120). 2022 and 2023 cannot tell. Nobody has asked whether this book is big enough to tell at all. Focus item 2 asks it, because it decides whether the director's six fresh seeds (EP17) can answer. The SLC 21B.4 read instruction, a licence duty, has had its switch-on predictions filed since 18 Oct and has never been run. It is focus item 1. The previous focus named 3 items, all 3 were drawn and all 3 landed (f04bd6102 and ec7fd9942, abe7ce533, 75aff1401 and d4af471a1), so all three leave focus. Two of this stretch's ticks were handed work another lane had already spent (711359a8c, 732b2e116).

## 2026-10-20 — Founders are 400 households and the settlement budget is 7,700, on a curve measured at that shape

<!-- head: 8ad5b62fbabf -->

**In plain English:** The supplier now opens in 2016 with a book of 400 households, and the run's budget was raised so they can all be settled.

**What changed.** Founders are now 400 households (`founder_unit: households`). At seed 20260724
that is 689 supply points. The settlement budget goes 5,000 → 7,700 customer-years. This acts on
the director's ruling of 20 Oct 17:40
(`docs/staging/advisor/done/DIRECTOR_RULING_FOUNDER_HOUSEHOLDS_WITH_BUDGET_RAISED_2026-10-20.md`).

**The budget, derived.** The 689 founder records commit 6,535.7 cy. The campaign had 1,206.5 cy of
room at the old shape, which gives 7,742.2, floored to 50 = 7,700. The campaign keeps 96.5% of its
room.

**The curve at the new shape** (`docs/observability/settlement_ceiling_slope_20261020.json`, both
points clean):

| Budget | Committed cy | Peak child RSS | Wall | Wins settled / funnel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7,000 | 6,997.2 | 4,444.3 MB | 7,247 s | 78 / 597 |
| 7,700 | 7,699.3 | 5,113.2 MB | 9,232 s | 205 / 597 |

The 7,700 peak plus the 227 MB parent is 5,340 MB. That is 668 MB under the 6,008 MB allowance
(0.25 × guest) and outside the pre-registered 5% stop line. The curve supports 8,638.6 cy. Run time
rises from 5,481 s (the 9 Oct curve at 5,000, supply points) to 9,232 s, ×1.68 for ×1.54 committed
cy. The pre-registration is graded beside its predictions (P1, P3, P4 hit; P2 missed low by 156 MB).
The probe stamped a salvage-commit head that no production run could carry; the landed copy names
`7858b89a6`, so the journal leg that carries his caveat can arm.

**Census, same seed, before (supply points, 5,000) → after (households, 7,700).**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Founder homes | 233 | 400 |
| Founder supply points | 400 | 689 |
| Founder dual-fuel share | 71.7% | 72.3% |
| Campaign quotes | 3,373 | 3,250 |
| Funnel wins | 619 | 597 |
| Settled campaign wins | 216 | 205 |
| Acquisition spend | £74,990.15 | £72,262.76 |

Settled wins by year, after: 32, 26, 21, 19, 23, 20, 8, 23, 22, 11 (2016–2025).

`tools/world_claims.py` was run on both books (8 seeds pooled, all three routes). Every claim holds
both before and after. Founders' dual share of homes is 76.4% → 76.0%, gas home share 84.9% →
84.9%, and direct-debit share 72.1% → 72.0%. This is the new held draw (EP17).

**Published figures it moves.** The opening book goes from 400 to 689 accounts, and the account
count everywhere moves with it. Quotes and acquisition spend go down. I have not attributed the
fall: a bigger book quoting fewer is the opposite of what happened on 9 Oct. Settled campaign wins
fall from 216 to 205.

**Still owed (his caveat).** Peak memory of the first three production runs at the new shape,
against 6,008 MB. If any run comes within 5% (above 5,708 MB), or the reaper fires, production
goes back to 400 supply points at 5,000. The continuation `founder-households-first-three-peaks`
carries this.

## 2026-10-20 — orientation: Forward on the supplier side, but it cannot yet show it beats the flat baseline, and one control on that baseline was found to prove nothing

<!-- head: b8045dd4e2ff -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-20T17:23:16.844326+00:00; 15 commits, 6 substantive, since 2026-10-20T14:21:15.441257+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 0 supplier, 1 world, 2 both, 12 other.

## What the stretch meant

Forward on the supplier side, but it cannot yet show it beats the flat baseline, and one control on that baseline was found to prove nothing. 15 commits, 6 substantive. The brief splits them 0 supplier, 1 world, 2 both, 12 other. That undercounts the supplier: most of the 'other' commits were supplier grades and records. Four supplier results moved. (1) B12 recorded L1 (455adef1a): writer one's renewal floor is built on the unit rate, with all three clauses reached from the run and each control mutation-proven. That is the stretch's only level move. (2) B8 Q8 (ee995aadc): the run's retention holdout now decides on expected value under a published-trial prior, as canon C8 rules ('build what you offered'). It is the first decision in the run that infers from published evidence rather than from a flat rule. At the founders' scale the company's own rows carry at most 0.002 of the weight, so the prior decides alone, and only 3-4 of 92 offers pay. (3) D48 (8902ff50b, 59ee65caf): the annual DD review now seeks the balance it finds by default, and it never seeks a balance its own rule already adds. (4) C35 graded R1-R4 CONFIRMED in its prereg: it rises 109 of 144 refused 2019 renewals, every rise inside the default's headroom, and the book is unmoved. Its engine caller is in surgical_land now (pid 847333). When that lands, every per-customer save, advice and retention decision has a production caller, behind switches that default off. What that means is the thesis's hard part. The machinery exists, and it decides almost nothing: C34 advises 4 of 972 renewals, the retention guard offers 9 times where it used to offer 92, and the median renewal still reads -GBP 3.91 a month for a reason nobody has measured. The previous item 2 was refused 49 times, because C35's own worktree holds the file that item only reads. Worse for the comparison the thesis needs, the flat supplier's reachability control has been unfalsifiable on origin since c61d8b608: both arms make 0 offers in 2016, so a flat arm leaking offers would look identical. A baseline whose control cannot fail is not yet a baseline to beat. Two corrections landed. The -GBP 100k net-margin move my last record carried as unattributed was two clocks differenced, provisioned against realised bad debt, and like for like the book moved +GBP 148 (cd1f976c7). And the Lane 0 re-issue of C35 and B12 worked: both were drawn, which corrects the seat's atom-id steer. The budget's second seed holds every band (b8045dd4e). Its default flip is under test, and the BLOCKING crisis bad-debt finding now waits on the first published run with the switches on. The previous focus reached the draw for 2 of 3 items. B12 is done and drops out. C35 is mid-landing, so it leaves focus as in hand. The -GBP 3.91 measurement comes back first.

## 2026-10-20 — orientation: Flat on the thesis, and the supplier side did not move

<!-- head: 254b4686a78d -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-20T14:21:15.441257+00:00; 6 commits, 2 substantive, since 2026-10-20T11:20:33.441434+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 0 supplier, 2 world, 0 both, 4 other.

## What the stretch meant

Flat on the thesis, and the supplier side did not move. 6 commits, 2 substantive, split 0 supplier, 2 world, 4 other. Both substantive commits were world builds taken by the ordinary draw (B7's job-loss scar, b1d3860b8; W2_36's half-hourly meter is read so C7 stops billing on estimates, 254b4686a, which bears on billing accuracy). Two supplier results were graded on the true margin. The retention guard's R1-R5 held (42d4e8e3d), with the net-margin move of -GBP 100,746 filed unattributed; its parent control is running. C34's P2' held on all four bands (b8c665948): on the term's contribution it advises 4 of 972 renewal rows, and the book is unmoved to the penny because the switch records only. What that means is the important part of this stretch. Now that every renewal decision reads one true margin, that margin says the median renewing household contributes -GBP 3.91 a month, and 85.8% of 324 households are negative, while the book's net margin is +GBP 446,884. With our side below zero on almost every renewal, no advice action can clear our floor, which is the director's open C34 concern in numbers. Until we know whether that negative contribution is the world's truth, a cost-to-serve allocation, or renewal prices set below cost, no per-customer decision can be shown to beat the flat baseline, so focus item 2 measures it. The steer drifted. C35 and B12 were named by atom id, and the draw had stopped taking C35, so neither was drawn; both come back as Lane 0 slices. The third item was drawn and done: the budget's second seed failed to start because setsid does not leave the executor's cgroup (4738f1cf5). Its off arm finished, and its shared arm is running for the 18:20 grade. That corrects the seat's own false launch record. No level moved. There is still no evidence on inference. The B8 published-trial prior is in hand in /var/tmp/se-b8-prior, and leg (b) of the leaver finding is in hand in /var/tmp/se-cos. The publisher's FAILING line is a stale episode: its cited red passes at HEAD, this week's figures reached origin on 19 Oct, and the next window opens on 26 Oct.

## What the stretch meant

Forward on correctness, not yet on inference. 4 commits, 1 substantive; the classifier reads 0 supplier, 0 world, 1 both and 3 other, and all of it was supplier work. All three focus items were drawn. C34's roll and riding leg now read the term's contribution, net of pass-through costs and cost to serve, instead of the spread over wholesale (a57ea3da0). The same fix for the live retention guard and the missed-retention log is in surgical_land now, with its base off arm running. That retires the VAT-shaped defect in four places, but it means no per-customer decision has yet been read on a true margin. The thesis claim that the supplier beats average by inference still has no evidence for or against it; what we have is a defect removed from under the evidence. C35's caller is pre-registered (49c24b74f) with its arms running. Leg (c) of the leaver finding was graded (5a2468fdf): C7 is billed within 0.956-1.025 of true use with no inversions, so the publish red is dead at HEAD and the 26 Oct publish is the test. Leg (b), closing on an estimate, is billing accuracy and goes into focus. The budget's second seed launched at 08:19Z. No level moved. The previous focus did bite: all three were drawn, and two are now live continuations, so they leave focus rather than being restated. One machine error is new: the brief said no long job launched this stretch, and the register shows one did.

## 2026-10-20 — orientation: Backwards on what we can claim, and that is the most useful result of the stretch

<!-- head: dd7809f23ecc -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-20T05:20:29.703610+00:00; 8 commits, 3 substantive, since 2026-10-20T02:20:32.195527+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 0 supplier, 1 world, 0 both, 7 other.

## What the stretch meant

Backwards on what we can claim, and that is the most useful result of the stretch. 8 commits, 3 substantive. The classifier reads 0 supplier, 1 world, 7 other, because the stretch's supplier work landed as grades and the classifier files grades as other. No level moved. The first full-book engine reading of a per-customer decision came back (86f1ef8f4): C34 at the renewal roll advised 11% of rows, P1-P3 refuted and P4 held. The grade then found why. The caller hands C34 (unit_rate - company_fwd) x EAC as 'margin', and that is the all-in tariff rate less the wholesale forward. It still carries network, policy and operating costs. The advised rows were all above GBP 30 a month, and 0 of 495 at or below GBP 30 were advised, so C34 advised because the margin was inflated, not because it inferred anything. That means the director's open C34 concern is still untested on the real book. Reading simulation/run_phase2b.py this orientation shows the same expression is the LIVE retention guard's expected_margin (~L3542), the riding leg (~L3330), the C34 roll (~L3521) and the missed-retention log (~L4064). Meanwhile company.interfaces.renewal_offer.term_cost_floor (forward + capital + locked policy + locked network) is already computed at the same roll, through _price_match_inputs. So every retention decision the company has made in production weighed an overstated value at stake. That is the VAT shape again: one quantity, four implementations, all wrong the same way. Elsewhere: the save offer's P1a was refuted on 9 decided rolls, P1b held, and the household carry was never exercised (bb93b4e8d). Its control is in surgical_land now (pid 3959362). The budget's shared-shortfall ordering removed the pre-crisis Q4 excess on one seed (2c361b329), and a second seed is owed before either switch can default on. Leg (c)'s HH files were regenerated (6de3afb10), and its grading run (run_annual_report on 27cb8d183, pid 3677477) is 52 minutes in. The baseline comparison the thesis needs (EP17, flat against per-customer) still waits on the director's seed listing. NONE of the previous focus was drawn under its own id. Items 1 and 3 were done anyway, under the live continuations they duplicated (read-the-c34-on-arm-r4-and-grade-p1-p4 and the-budget-orders-energy-...), so that steer was redundant rather than ignored. That was the seat's error, and it is corrected here: no focus row restates a queued continuation, and item 1 subsumes c34-renewal-margin-net-of-pass-through explicitly. C35, the one genuine ask, went undrawn behind the continuations. It stays in focus, now behind the margin fix, so it is not built on the wrong quantity.

## What the stretch meant

The supplier moved this stretch, and the honest answer to the thesis question is now on the record: cannot tell. B11's within-segment term (27ca9dc7a) replaced the whole-book figure, two-thirds of which was flat's own inverted gas segment. Per-customer clears flat only at 2020, and only by a hair (+0.061, interval +0.002 to +0.120 on 8b6fea024; +0.065 on ad8afadc5). At 2022 and 2023 it cannot tell. That is not backwards: it says the earlier reading overclaimed. A powered answer needs the varied draws, and c52f83113 made every seed-family member stamp its own grade and pool it. So the binding constraint on the thesis test is now the director's seed listing (ep17), not code. C34 got the first engine caller of the three per-customer decisions (18503313a), off by default and byte-identical off. On the short window it decides 32 households and advises 1, and our floor refuses 95 of 96 rows. So the director's open C34 concern is now an engine reading, not a harness one. The gas-leg probe closed the dual-fuel re-take (dd35d2a18): per-household C35 changes how many decisions are made, not the rescue rate. Both items the last record re-issued as Lane 0 were drawn and landed, which corrects the steer that had drifted at 14:22. The third item, the budget floor, was not drawn. The seat's own new error: it called the HH-EAC leg (d) grade queued when its continuation had lapsed, so the BLOCKING leaver finding had no route. It leads focus now, on the run already going (59e1658d6 carries 6208ea6dd). Split: supplier 1, both 1, world 3, other 6. The world commits were the director's constant-anchoring reading, which is his call. dd35d2a18 sits on HEAD and not on origin, which is the divergence the brief reports. Its grade is counted here as evidence, but nothing downstream of origin can see it until it is pushed. Corrected this stretch: the dual-fuel re-take, the B11 split, and the stalled atom-id steer.

The thesis did not move this stretch. The one supplier commit was small but real. The dual-fuel offset (SLC 27.8D) is now on for every standing policy (3d518bdef). Both are re-issued below as Lane 0 items. The stretch instead answered the director's two live questions. On 'Is dual fuel sorted?': of three default-off switches, one went on, one stays off for the budget's chronic heads excess, and one is unwired. On 400 founder households: they fit in memory, but at budget 5,000 they leave the campaign no win in any year. That is raised as a reserved concern with a recommendation (019924a77). ## 2026-10-19 — 400 founder households fit in memory; the switch waits on the settlement budget, which they exhaust by themselves

<!-- head: c57d93ba5b5e -->

**In plain English:** Before the opening book grew to 400 households, it was measured to fit in this machine's memory.

**The director's 19 Oct 16:37 ruling, "Households, as long as it doesn't create a memory problem".**
Measured the cheap way (R8): two founders-only points, run one after the other through
`launch_long_job`, with the reaper untouched.
- 100 homes: 1,906 MB, 1,241 s.
- 200 homes: 2,656 MB, 2,682 s.
- A cgroup anon sampler agrees with the child's own figure.
Today's production run (`ad8afadc5`) gives a third point: 4,065 MB.

**Census, seed 20260724.** Today: 400 records = 233 homes, 167 dual (0.717), 3,794 committed cy.
At 400 homes: 697 records, 296 dual (0.738), 6,603 committed cy.

**Branch: it fits.** About 4,180 MB at today's budget, or about 5,350–5,540 MB with the budget
raised to keep the campaign's room, against a 6,008 MB allowance.

**The switch is held.** At today's 5,000-cy budget the founders alone exceed it, so the campaign
would be admitted no win in any year. That consequence was not in the ruling. It is raised as
`your-400-household-founder-ruling-fits-in`, recommending households with the budget raised to
about 7,800. That is the logic of his 9 Oct approval.

**Published figures it would move.** Nothing has moved. On the switch, every book figure moves:
homes 233 → 401 founders, and supply points about +300. The world claims and the EP17 held draw
are re-recorded then.

**Predictions.** Four of five were wrong. A ~1,160 MB fixed base and campaign customer-years
costing twice founder ones are what I did not know. Graded in
`docs/staging/records/SEAT_PREREG_WHAT_400_FOUNDER_HOUSEHOLDS_COST_IN_MEMORY_AND_TIME_MEASURED_ON_SMALL_BOOKS_2026-10-19.md`.

## 2026-10-19 — orientation: The evidence for the thesis went backwards this stretch, and the stretch found out why

<!-- head: 3e0f624a6f16 -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-19T14:22:11.308976+00:00; 15 commits, 6 substantive, since 2026-10-19T11:22:12.315300+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 1 world, 1 both, 12 other.

## What the stretch meant

The evidence for the thesis went backwards this stretch, and the stretch found out why. The reading the seat carried as proof that inference beats a flat baseline was B11's whole-book clearance, +0.133 at 2023. Two-thirds of it was flat's own defect: the gas segment was inverted, so flat ranked worse than chance at 0.409 (4958a4945). The key itself did not get worse; its AUC rose from 0.580 to 0.592 on the dual book. But within segments it is +0.108 old and +0.075 new over chance, with no interval, so today nobody can say it clears flat. Item 2 builds that term. The second finding is larger. No engine path makes a C34 or C35 decision (60c4814af). The per-household switch-on (f6e23a535) is correct and changes no run. Every per-customer advice and retention decision the thesis describes exists only inside harness tools, so no run can yet show per-customer against flat on them. Item 3 gives C34 a caller, off by default. C35 re-taken on the dual book reads 144 of 546 rescued, but it is costed on electricity alone, and the probe fix that adds the gas leg is being built in /var/tmp/se-seat-executor. World work landed where it blocks supplier results. The HH-EAC registration landed (6208ea6dd), which is the cause of the BLOCKING leaver finding. U1-U4 hold for the budget exit (a1235d427), though a chronic heads excess keeps that switch off. The B7 sole-occupant death exit landed (e0b301545). The split was supplier 1, world 1, both 1, other 12, and the one supplier commit changed no decision. The machine is the immediate block. The shared checkout has been stuck at ad8afadc5 since 09:24Z, 24 commits behind. The publish re-arm (ba8f179ce) is therefore inert in the worker that would use it, and the run now going lacks HH-EAC, so it cannot clear the leaver rows. Item 1 clears this. All three previous focus items were drawn and all three landed, so they leave focus. Corrected this stretch: C35's per-leg rise, the switch-on that lapsed unseen, and the under-water budget.

## What the stretch meant

The block cleared, and what it uncovered is a step back for the thesis. Behind it was the first per-customer reading taken on households GB actually has. The 19 Oct dual-fuel book is on origin (2a195224b, merged f8f3d0fd5). It went out by hand: the publisher never retried it after its red was answered, so that wrong row's instance is closed and its class is not. Both previous focus items are finished and leave focus. The B11 grade (f00fdb040) is the reading that matters. On the dual book, the per-customer switch key against flat at 2023 over the whole book is +0.075 (-0.013, +0.162) on 201 graded households. It was +0.133 and cleared on the 1%-dual book. So the one clearance the thesis had for inference over the whole book is gone, and only movers at 2023 still clear. P0 held: no supplier change moved B11 between the two runs, so the book's fuel mix did this, not our code. Whether the signal is weaker on dual homes or just noisier on a smaller sample is not yet known, and that is item 2. The other gradings came back like this. The leaver grade (b139ed649) found the C7 class's cause in the world: half-hourly roster accounts register no EAC, so C7 is billed at a 3,100 kWh TDCV against 13,230 kWh true. The read duty is not the cause; it reaches only 22 of 275 legs. That world fix is landing now through surgical_land, with its grade queued. The budget-decides-payment build was graded (c43df1237) and refuted high: under-water households never left it. An exit was added at DWP's published rate (78a36a84c), the switch stays off, and the on arm is being re-captured now. The campaign now wins split homes at 90.6% dual (30246d6f0). The split was supplier 0, world 4, other 13. Every substantive commit was world fidelity or the grading of it. Each one blocked a named supplier result (the publish, the leaver, the payment draw), but supplier code did not move this stretch. One seat error came to light: the per-household next-best-action switch-on, which the 08:23 record said was queued, is in no live queue. The 23:21 orientation embargoed it nine hours out, past the six-hour expiry, so it lapsed unseen, and the 08:23 record never asked live(). It is item 1. The previous focus was drawn and both items landed. The held-estimate row closes: the published book now carries the fix. The campaign-dual row closes on 30246d6f0.

## 2026-10-19 — orientation: The machine delivered this stretch, and the thesis did not move, because the one thing everything waits on did not happen

<!-- head: 7549b0a095ad -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-19T08:23:26.318960+00:00; 9 commits, 5 substantive, since 2026-10-19T05:22:33.070254+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 0 world, 1 both, 7 other.

## What the stretch meant

The machine delivered this stretch, and the thesis did not move, because the one thing everything waits on did not happen. Seven commits carried work. Two of the previous focus items are finished and leave focus. The director's 19 Oct knowledge steer landed in full: 446 bare world constants registered (7cb23588e), population pages that carry claims the drawn world is checked against (cb38f8ca4), and the two Low Carbon tables shown to be two sourced facts (7549b0a09). The dual household's SLC 27.8D offset is built, default off (b529875b1). The payment draw's price input is landing right now through surgical_land, with its paired capture arms still running. The split was supplier 1, both 1, other 7, world 0. So supplier work was thin, but nothing went to world fidelity that blocks no result. The checks also earned their keep at once: the claim check found that the campaign route wins every gas home as dual (100% against a published 81-96%), a new world wrong row now in hand. Against the thesis, though, the stretch went nowhere, and my 05:22 record was wrong. It said the first published dual-fuel book would be on origin within the hour. The publish commit was refused at 06:35Z by the defect4 gate on one leaver, C7: a never-read, closed-on-estimate account billed at 23% of its true use. The gate was answered at 06:56Z (dc4dc0e10), and the publisher's state now reads the cited red as DEAD at HEAD. But nothing has re-attempted the publish in the 1.5h since, and nothing will: the marker is archived, and the retry waits for an identical run that is not queued. Origin's run output is still the 13 Oct book, 130h old. So the grade of both preregs, the closing of three carried wrong rows (the held estimate, the 1%-dual figures, the C35 per-leg charge), the per-household switch-on, and every per-customer figure the thesis is judged on are all parked behind one re-drive. That is item 1. Item 2 is the supplier question the refusal raised. C7 is not a gate problem. 274 of 405 churned legs now close on an estimate, and the company's read duty is off in the standing policy. Billing accuracy is first in the director's order, and which of the three filed explanations is true is settled by measuring, not by switching something on. The previous focus was steered: 3 of 5 drawn. Item 3 was refused 10 times because the executor's own worktree held its paths, and that was the item being worked, not a wrong refusal. The flat-supplier baseline (EP17/B11) is built and still waits on the director's seed listing, so whether per-customer beats flat can still be neither said nor refuted.
