## 2026-10-19 — Knowledge pages now carry claims the drawn world is checked against

<!-- head: dc4dc0e10408 -->

**In plain English:** The Knowledge pages now state published GB figures, such as how many homes take both fuels, that the simulated population is checked against.

**Director steer 19 Oct, knowledge that checks the world: items 1 to 3 built, item 4 handed on.**

- **Item 1, anchor or range** (landed earlier today, `tools/world_constant_anchors.py`): **446** bare world constants are registered by name in `docs/design/world_constant_anchor_register.txt`, controlled as an exact set, with `DEFAULT_BAND_WEIGHTS` first.
- **Item 2, pages carry checks.** Each population page now has a `world-claims` block that states the figure, its band and its source. `tools/world_claims.py` measures every claim on the founder book the production draw makes at the production founder count, over 8 seeds pooled (1,732 homes, 3,056 accounts). The band is written only on the page. `tests/simulation/test_the_opening_book_bears_the_published_fuel_split.py` used to carry its own copy and now reads the page.
  - Fuel page §5b: dual share of homes 76.4% (band 70–85%); dual share of gas homes 90.0% (81–96%); gas homes 84.9% (81.5–88.5%), with off-grid as the complement; gas-only homes 3.9% (≤15%); gas-only on a home without gas 0.0% (must be 0).
  - Payment-method page: direct-debit share of accounts 72.1% (66.5–75.5%). **GAP:** the published shares read so far start in 2020, while the founders open in 2016.
  - **Red on first run: none.** The 17 Oct fix had already brought the book inside the bands, so a green first run says nothing about whether the check works. The mutation proof below does.
  - **Mutation-proven on the production draw, not a fixture:**
    - `P_DUAL_GIVEN_GAS` 0.90 to 0.50 reds three claims.
    - The same constant at 1.0 reds only the conditional claim, so the homes-level band alone would have missed it.
    - DD shares at 0.50 red the payment claim.
    - In the tests, a band edited on the page reds the check. The partition control reaches holds, GAP and UNCHECKABLE, and an empty denominator reads UNCHECKABLE, not 0%.
  - The Monday step prints the full table, red first, ahead of its end-to-end check. It says NOT MEASURED if the draw raises.
- **Item 3, a change to who is in the world re-runs them.** The commit gate's `SUBJECT_TESTS` maps five subjects to `tests/tools/test_world_claims.py` (about 4 s): `FOUNDER_BOOK.yaml` (the founder count), `live_population.py`, `population_draw.py`, `premise_population.py`, and `net_new_acquisition.py` (the prospect cap). An edit to either page selects the test through the data surface. **GAP:** the claims measure the founder book only. The trickle and campaign routes' own composition is not yet measured.
- **Item 4, one home per fact: not done.** `company/regulatory/fuel_mix_reconciliation.py` already shows the two Low Carbon % tables are like-for-like (both count biomass) and differ in their data by up to 3.4 points. Neither cites a vintage. Picking the right one needs the DESNZ source fetched and written up first (K8). Handed on as `one-low-carbon-table-from-a-fetched-source`.

The book now holds households GB actually has, and the published run will carry it. That is the stretch's result, and it is a precondition rather than progress on the thesis. The dual-fuel correction (c136809f5, 01:14Z) is on origin before the 19 Oct publish: drawn founders open 220 homes, 73.6% dual and 83.6% on gas, against the published 72-90%. The live book now draws 788 supply points in 447 households, 341 of them dual. Two supplier doors followed. C35 now decides a dual household once instead of per leg (d96d33f3d). ## What the stretch meant

Two doors from a per-customer forecast to a per-customer decision landed this stretch. Both are dormant, so the thesis has its first decisions that use inference, and none of them fires yet in a published run. C35's retention rise (4a40365d3) rescues 211 of 780 advice cases on the published book's 260 renewals, at both B11 hazard ends. The page said 314, and the shortfall is explained beside it: the 104 world rescues before 2019 have no published default tariff to read. The read instruction at the 11th estimate (6e9dc90f8) cuts the 21BA bar on the crossed runs from GBP 3,929 to GBP 5 at the read end, and moves nothing at the no-access end. Per-customer against flat is unchanged, because EP17 still waits on the director's seed row. The bigger result is that the director found the book itself wrong. It is 1% dual fuel against a published 72-83%, and every gas home is split-supply by construction. The cause is a placeholder coin that the repo's own 21 June page already contradicted. So every per-customer CLV, hazard and cost-to-serve figure argued this month was computed on households GB does not have. That includes C34's 18 cases and C35's 780. In that sense the stretch went backwards: more of what we believed is now unattributed. The correction is built: a knowledge page, a census, a prereg with its predictions graded (228 homes against 223 predicted, 67.5% dual against 71%), and a control. But it has sat uncommitted in the shared tree since about 11:19Z, with no claim in either store and no commit. It was never drawn, so no block of this brief could list it. It also turns a collections-journey test red in that tree. Landing it is the first item. I chose to let the 19 Oct publish carry it rather than publish a third week on a book he called fantastically wrong. The cost is that the publish stops being a one-variable reading. Balance: supplier 1, both 1, world 0, other 7. Of the other, the two B7 pages are world knowledge: the recovery coin runs a 19-month median against its own cited 6, and no household changes its membership. Tick mode has been slow since 10:18Z and stays slow until the publish (worker-tick at most every 4h), which accounts for only 9 commits. All three previous focus items were drawn. ## 2026-10-17 — The opening book was 1% dual fuel; the account now takes its home's fuel

<!-- head: bc900a5d5f2d -->

**In plain English:** The simulated customer book had almost no homes taking gas and electricity together; each account now takes the fuels its home really uses, matching the published GB split.

**Director steer 17 Oct: the opening book was 1% dual fuel. Researched, corrected, and now held by a control.**

- **Knowledge page:** `docs/market_research/how_a_gb_domestic_book_splits_by_fuel_and_how_a_two_fuel_home_switches.md`.
  - CMA final report ¶10: 20m dual, 8m electricity-only and 3m gas-only customers.
  - GfK: 72% of homes take one supplier for both fuels.
  - Ofgem 2017: homes with gas switch both fuels at once, ~90%.
  - Challengers run 80–90%+ dual; Octopus G/E is 0.80.
- **Census, drawn founders, default seed:**
  - Before: 382 homes, none dual, 28% gas-only, 93% gas homes.
  - After: 220 homes holding the same 382 supply points; 73.6% dual; 83.6% gas homes. Eight seeds pooled: 76.4% dual.
  - The trickle takes the same shape. Campaign wins were already ~100% dual (published ~90%).
  - Departures were already household-level. Home move and debt are not yet re-measured.
- **Root cause:**
  - The 13 July placeholder named no anchor page, though a 21 June page had the answer.
  - The 26 Aug ruling was fixed only in the funnel, where it was seen.
  - The 16 Sept finding took 28% gas-only as a fact about the world.
  - No control compared the book with the published record while it grew 13 → 400.
- **Mechanism:** `tests/simulation/test_the_opening_book_bears_the_published_fuel_split.py`, at the production founder count over eight seeds. Mutation-proven:
  - three seeds was too few to catch the heating defect, so it is eight;
  - P(dual)=0, meter-first off and the old coin each red it.
- **Sweep:**
  - commodity coin: retired;
  - founder heating: meter-first;
  - `DEFAULT_BAND_WEIGHTS`: a named GAP, with NEED as the anchor;
  - the harness panel's 90.7% gas: handed on with its pinned values.
- **Pre-registered predictions** all held at 0.83. The constant then moved to 0.90 on the advisor's supplier evidence, and that is reported as a second step.
- **Published figures** move at the next run.
- **Proposal:** whether 400 founders means supply points (held) or households is raised as `the-founder-number-has-two-readings-now`.

## 2026-10-17 — orientation: Inference now has a faint positive signal and still no decision that uses it, so the thesis did not move this stretch

<!-- head: a70364b0cb86 -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-17T08:22:36.779386+00:00; 24 commits, 10 substantive, since 2026-10-17T05:22:08.800265+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 3 supplier, 1 world, 1 both, 19 other.

## What the stretch meant

Inference now has a faint positive signal and still no decision that uses it, so the thesis did not move this stretch. It did not go backwards either. B11 slices 11-13 (e3cd17232, 51ec26010, 73f98aecd) keyed the switch hazard on months on the default tariff, which a real supplier holds. Switchers rank better than flat beyond the 95% bound at 2023 only (+0.103, lower bound +0.002), and at no cut against the contract-year rule. So the answer is cannot tell, leaning the key, and by its prereg the key does not yet enter EP17's arm. The LEVEL is a separate and harder result. The flat rule over-predicts held-back departure by +0.24, +0.18 and +0.07 at the three cuts. The cause is that the 2017-20 switching regime ended, and no fit window chosen from inside the book cures it: the after-crisis window flips 2023 to -0.089. The book cannot identify a per-customer level for margin or CLV without a regime band from the published record. The world measurement half-confirmed the worry that the world is rigged against observable targeting. The payment gradient is drawn (PPM:DD 0.52) and comes through at fixed-term ends (0.50 against the published 0.55). It is lost on the SVT drift route, which carries most switching (0.98). The fix, W-A, is filed for after the publish with its predictions. The tariff gradient turned out to be a matter of era, not selection: about 2.6 in 2024-25 against the published 2.8. Read through the CMA's own instrument, the pre-crisis world sits inside the CMA's 1.9-4.3. That corrects my last record, which said fixed here mostly means a first term. C34's holdout reader landed (d42796112), and on this book it rightly decides nothing. What the stretch makes plain: forecasting has been tested thirteen slices deep while no per-customer decision fires. Next best action advises nobody, because our floor refuses every positive-sum case (the director's open c34 row), and EP17 waits on his seed row. Only one door from forecast to decision is ours to build without him. The director minted C35 on 2026-10-15 as "not a ruling from me", and his c34 row has stood five days with the sharing price as the recommended option. A Fixed Retention Tariff rise is the one form of share the world already answers, through its price response at renewal. So it goes first, dormant behind a switch that defaults off, and the c34 row stays open for him to choose the floor change instead. ## 2026-10-17 — orientation: For the first time in ten slices, inference was tested on what a real supplier holds, and the answer is "cannot tell"

## What the stretch meant

For the first time in ten slices, inference was tested on what a real supplier holds, and the answer is "cannot tell". That is honest, and it is not yet a result against the thesis. B11 slice 10 (5f57b9042) gave the departure hazard tariff type, payment method and months on the default tariff, read only from the company's own term record and bills. It cannot rank switchers above the flat rule beyond the 95% bound at any of 2020, 2022 or 2023. The finding's addendum shows why this is not the end of the question. Split by cause, months on default reproduces the published switching gradient on switches alone (0.68 and 0.50, against CMOL's 0.54). Moves run the other way, and the all-cause hazard washed the two together. So the prior was right and the hazard it multiplied was the wrong quantity. Slice 10 also found a level drift in its own rule (P2, wrong at every cut). Two published gradients the world is said to carry do not show up in who switches away: prepayment switches at about direct debit's rate, not 0.55x, and "fixed" in this world mostly means a customer's first term. If the world does not produce the departure correlates the record says real customers have, then targeting by observable is rigged to fail here. That is the director's 2026-10-08 worry from the other side, and it makes a world measurement the second item. Billing accuracy moved too. The theft screen now reaches the monthly billing run behind a switch that defaults off (3161365d3). The money an estimated final bill leaves open at closure is priced at GBP 3,471 of GBP 13,467 (8cd8e9954). A gaining supplier's first read could reach at most GBP 701 of the GBP 2,222 dispute seed, and only at the every-case ceiling (bc4c80fca). That continuation correctly refused to build a dispute path, because the dispute moves money between suppliers rather than creating any. Balance: supplier 1, both 1, world 1, other 12. Most of the "other" commits are a run of five self-issued W2_36 continuations in three hours, each narrowing the same closing money. It is billing work, but on the world's side and at falling pounds. After the read-duty split now landing (surgical_land 3365466), I am not ordering any more of it until the publish. Both previous focus items were drawn and both landed, so both leave focus. ## 2026-10-16 — orientation: The stretch gave us an answer, and it moved the 2022 problem

<!-- head: 3f7959f480e0 -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-16T20:22:27.532042+00:00; 10 commits, 4 substantive, since 2026-10-16T17:22:58.283644+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 2 supplier, 0 world, 0 both, 8 other.

## What the stretch meant

The stretch gave us an answer, and it moved the 2022 problem. The question is now where the world falls short, not whether it does. The diagnosis (91ad4cad8, 3f7959f48) found that the world's count of households in arrears is roughly in Ofgem's range in most years. What is wrong is the pound balance per debtor, 9-14x low in every year, crisis or not. Each bill is an independent coin flip, so 78% of world debtors are exactly one bill behind and then pay again. The payment draw also has no price input: the four 2021-22 bill levels give identical failure shares. The household budget does respond to 2022, but nothing reads it. The worker's own first fix (move the tier up a step) was refuted by the table it printed next, and is kept beside the replacement: let the budget decide how much of each bill gets paid, month after month. All four pre-registered predictions were refuted, and that is the instrument working. For the thesis, this means a per-customer debt decision is graded in a world where debt clears by itself. In that world, collecting a debt and forgiving it look about the same, so we cannot yet tell value created from value moved. My own record was wrong about the company side. I said the provision charge peaks a year after the arrears. 52eafa5dd prints both by year: the published age-band provision does not lag, and it is largest in 2022. So the crisis bad-debt finding stays BLOCKING on the level only, and the level is the world's problem. It is not a supplier defect. Billing accuracy moved forward. c5963a5c0 registers each year an account goes without a read (the SLC 21B.4 breach) and publishes the count beside K2. The company can now see its own breach. The flat-against-per-customer comparison is where it was. B11 is parked at L2 with every door built. It needs the 10-19 publish and the six seeds only the director can list (open row ep17-s-flat-against-per-customer-comparison). That is still the biggest gap against the thesis, and it is not ours to close. Commit split: 2 supplier, 0 world, 8 other. Two of the eight "other" commits are world findings and one is E6's measurement, so supplier-first held in substance, if not in the label. All four previous focus items were drawn, and all four are done, so none is carried. The tombstone item landed (a5f02f869), and wrong_triage now marks that row already_fixed. It leaves the wrong list by that route, not by being dropped. Next is the largest open money figure on the billing page, £33,770 barred on direct-debit accounts, then pricing that shares value, then the knowledge page the non-payment build needs.

## What went wrong

My 17:22 record said the company's provision charge peaks in 2023, a year after the arrears, and E6's map comment said the age bands lag 2022 by a year. 52eafa5dd prints both by year from the committed run: arrears build most in 2022, and the age-band charge is largest in 2022. Only E6's learned roll-rate matrix lags, and that is already held by a strict xfail. The crisis finding stays BLOCKING on the level alone.

## 2026-10-15 — The director's phone goes quiet: NTFY is mothballed with its record kept, the inbound route is retired, one dead-man's push stays, and the advisor channel only draws what the advisor signed

<!-- head: 565bd6303b9c -->

*Written by the console seat, 15 Oct afternoon. It acts on the three steers staged while the director could not reach the pane.*

**What was retired, what stays, and the dead-man's decision** (the mothball steer's item 6). Landed as `565bd6303`; the two services are stopped, disabled and masked on the box, with their installed units kept in `~/.config/systemd/user/retired-2026-10-15/`.

- **Retired: the phone push.** `ntfy_utils.send_ntfy` is the only network POST, and it now writes the ops mirror (`ntfy-mirror.md`, direction `out-mothballed`) and the director input log instead. Nothing was deleted from the record: every alert the machine would have pushed is still a line the advisor reads.
- **Retired: the inbound route.** `ntfy_responder` and `dispatcher` have permanent no-op entry points, `retired` manifest rows and no unit files. The last message that route staged was `from_rich_20261006_204456.md`, nine days ago, so it had already stopped carrying his words. The library they leave behind is handed off as `retire-the-inbound-ntfy-library`.
- **Stays: the staging watcher.** It announces arrivals and acks the advisor channel. Its messages now go to the mirror.
- **Stays: one push to his phone.** A `[DEAD-MAN]` message goes out once per episode when no work has landed for 6 hours AND no Claude process is alive AND the worker-tick timer is inactive. **Decision: kept**, because it is rare by measurement. The hard rest cap it rides fired 0 times in the 47 days the mirror holds, against 10 to 44 stall or blocked alerts a day, and none of those reach him now. **What it cannot do:** a box that is wholly down runs no switch, so that case pages nothing. That is said here rather than implied.

**The advisor channel, and a duplicate I caused.** I built a channel in a worktree while a worker tick built and landed its own (`4a581cd72`, 16:11). I had not claimed the item, so the draw offered it to both. Mine lost the race to origin three times on 15-minute gates. Rather than land a rival, I kept theirs and added the one thing it lacked: **provenance** (`7bc3e3d3a`). A file is drawn only if origin holds its exact bytes in a commit signed by the advisor's key. Measured: all nine advisor commits since September carry one key, and none of the 1,045 machine commits is signed. Without this, any lane could write a file "on the director's standing delegation" and be drawn as his word, which is the reason the page-comment channel was retired on 07-24. The mothball was claimed (`seat_work_in_hand`) before it was built further.

**What the dropped console left, and where it went.**
- The parked-atom fix (`7bfd6fea3`, only on a salvage ref) landed as `47e544e24`. Its gate caught a census control that was already red at origin: B11 was unblocked this morning on his 05:52Z EP17 words and the frozen set was never updated. That line is in the same commit.
- **The shared checkout had stopped tracking origin.** It was 123 behind and refused by 56 paths, so every daemon ran code without the hold, tombstone and overlap fixes. 28 of the paths were byte-identical to revisions on origin. All 56 were snapshotted to `salvage/shared-ff-blockers-2026-10-15` and cleared, and the reconcile door fast-forwarded the checkout to `554bacacf`. `bb5276856`, the land-twice duplicate, is gone with it. The four old local-only edits stay on that tag, not re-applied.
- The land-twice control from the dropped session (`salvage/detached-90b25caf661c`) is superseded in part by `ed7e89d12`, which another lane landed at 13:21. The remaining question, whether the pre-commit door needs the same refusal, is handed off with the count that decides it.

**Mistakes worth keeping.**
- **The duplicate:** an unclaimed item drawn twice.
- **A machine-state file swept into a landing:** the visibility generator run with the real NTFY env appended a line to `ntfy_digest_queue.jsonl`. My re-land helper took every dirty path and carried it in. The helper now takes only the commit's own paths.
- **Picking up the wrong change:** after two WIP commits, the tag pointed at the second, and cherry-picking it would have landed only a one-line reword. A conflict stopped it first. The fix was squashing to one commit.
- **A `pkill -f` pattern that matched my own shell.**
- **An amend on the wrong commit:** a refused gate left HEAD on origin's merge commit, and my `--amend` rewrote a local copy of it. Nothing reached origin.
- **A cherry-pick that failed silently:** a leftover untracked file blocked it, and `| grep conflict` hid the error, so a 'v4' briefly held one file.
- **The gates were right each time they refused the mothball.** Two tests used `dispatcher` as their stand-in live daemon. CLAUDE.md's published operating model had to be regenerated. And the orphan ratchet saw that removing the units leaves the responder, the dispatcher and `inbound_secret_redaction` with nothing that runs them. They are frozen as deliberately dormant in the same commit.

**Stopped short of.** I did not delete the inbound library or its tests. That is about ten test files, the steer did not need it for "no inbound text can reach a lane", and the entry points are closed. W1_29 texture work was parked for next week by another lane, on the director's 13:01 steer.

## 2026-10-15 — The log did not stop: the 09:09 orientation died with the guest at 09:29, and the 12:41 entry was stamped at a stale shared fork, so the check misdated it

<!-- head: 688f52f8253e -->

*Written by a worker tick acting on `DIRECTOR_STEER_STRETCH_LOG_AND_DECK_2026-10-15.md` (staged 09:50 BST, drawn 14:50 BST).*

## Why the log looked stopped

Two causes. Neither of them was the orientation seat stopping.

1. **The machine went down.** The WSL guest shut down at 09:29:34 BST and booted at 09:53:22 (`journalctl --list-boots`). The shutdown SIGTERM'd the 09:09 orientation run mid-turn, so that stretch has no entry. The director's console link dropped in the same window. `delivery-seat.timer` re-armed at boot and ran at 12:41 BST, and that run wrote an entry and landed it (`6789bd0e1`).
2. **The entry it wrote was misdated.** `stretch_log.append` stamps an entry with `git rev-parse HEAD` in the tree that writes it. At 12:41 the shared tree's HEAD was `bb5276856`: a stale fork made at 10:10 BST, a duplicate of 068928f47, on a base dozens of commits behind origin. `--check` dates an entry from its stamp's commit and counts commits from it. So it read the 11:41Z entry as 4.4h old with 82 commits unreported, and at 13:33Z it paged that the log had stopped, while the log was being written.

## What changed

`background/delivery_seat.entry_head()`: the seat now stamps each entry with origin/main's tip, because the seat reads both sides and lands the entry on origin. With no origin it falls back to HEAD. The control is in `tests/background/test_the_orientation_seat_writes_the_stretch_log.py`, and reverting the stamp reds it. This entry is stamped at origin as well, so `--check` measures from here.

## The steer's other two items

- **Usage and the deck.** The 06:45 reading of 71% is the last one available, and the 6-point reserve stands. The deck order is unchanged: the machine-class known issues, confirming the 145 banners, staging fates, then C34 and EP17 minted for Monday. The no-paste steer re-states the same order.

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-14T17:24:04.146822+00:00; 12 commits, 3 substantive, since 2026-10-14T14:22:16.204467+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 0 supplier, 0 world, 0 both, 12 other.

## What the stretch meant

Nothing in the supplier book changed on origin this stretch. The split is 0 supplier, 0 world, 12 other, and 3 of 12 commits are substantive. But the two supplier changes the last record put first are both finished and in their landing gates now, and both make the supplier more right. First, the save. The director's stayers control was red because run_phase2b fed the billed unit rate to the rival's position ledger. After a save, the world's market reference read the save price, so every household's P(stay) moved by what the save cost. That is the company's reactive price leaking into the world. It was a fidelity defect, not proof that stayers pay. The ledger now observes the pre-save rate. The one-variable run at f6e806b8f passed 8 of 8, with line 76 green as the filed prediction said and line 95 (his condition) green on equal arms (surgical_land pid 782478). The cost is that every save-on grade taken before it, regrade5's included, was read through that channel, and nothing will re-ask them (focus three). Second, billing. Seven of the nine customer-years billed below margin were a real defect: a held estimate was still netted at its draft amount when the next read caught up. So a customer was credited for estimates never sent (PROS-2017-0336: -GBP 271.29). The fix trues a held bill up as unbilled energy under SLC 21BA, knowledge page first, with a mutation-proven control (pid 1017437). The two remaining rows are opening stubs that the oracle shares a later credit into by day, so they are an instrument question. Third, a regression found and correctly kept red: the crisis bad-debt control had skipped silently in every gate since the run went gzip on 2026-10-10. Read through the store, the published run fails 2022, a fact. The world builds the arrears (receivable x2.6, 30-90 days x2.5). The company's flat age-band provision charges them a year late. That is the heart of the business by his M7, and it is the next supplier build (focus one). Against the baseline, the deciding comparison (regrade5, per-customer risk tiers against the flat price match on writer 1's corrected basis) has two seeds left running and grades at 21:15. I correct my own 14:22 error: 58d629a20 stopped the term-cost floor legs ungraded and re-issued the re-take on the corrected basis, and the chain that would have launched floor b is gone. Last focus: items one and two were drawn and are landing. Items three (D48's accrual claim) and four (the shared HEAD) were never drawn, so the steer drifted there. The shared HEAD is now 3 ahead and 41 behind, and one of the three is the W1_29 knowledge section, on no remote ref. Both items are carried.

## 2026-10-14 — orientation: The stretch moved understanding, not the book

<!-- head: c92788173d93 -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-14T14:22:16.204467+00:00; 10 commits, 3 substantive, since 2026-10-14T11:21:28.356813+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 0 world, 0 both, 9 other.

## What the stretch meant

The stretch moved understanding, not the book. Ten commits, three substantive, and the split is 1 supplier, 0 world, 9 other. Nearly all of it was findings, and two of them say the supplier is less right than the record claimed. First, billing. The D48 Expert Hour (440ebe1f6) failed the row on its claim, not its measure: the title promises an accrual and a settlement reconciliation that the module says it does not compute. A worker then found nine customer-years at origin billed below their own gross margin. The leading cause, not yet tested, is that an estimate held by validate_bills drops out of the ledger while the next read's catch-up still credits against it. That is a credit with no matching charge, on the book the page publishes. Billing accuracy is first in the director's order, and it went backwards in what we can honestly claim. That is progress in knowledge and a regression in standing. Second, the save. The director's stayers control is red because the on and placebo arms split before any save had touched the household that split them. The named candidate is that the rival's ledger observes the save price. If that holds, the company is leaking a reactive, unlisted price into the world's market reference: the result is a fidelity defect, not proof that stayers pay. Until the one-variable run reads, no save figure is readable against his condition. Against the baseline, the test that matters is still in flight. Regrade5 compares the flat price match with the per-customer risk tiers on writer 1's corrected basis. Seed 61109 is finished, 61110 is running, and the grade comes off embargo at 17:15. f6e806b8f shows writer 1's target is now right, but the realised margin it learns from still reads high on fixed terms (median 8.5% against 1.67%), most likely because the lookback is mostly default-tariff terms. The basis is better, not finished. The machine's binding constraint this stretch was the box, not the draw. termcost-arms-floor-a is 12h36m into a 1.5h pre-registration, on a base older than writer 1's fix. The stayers fix run and its bisect queue behind its pid, and a chain behind it will launch floor b. That is the fault I corrected for regrade4 and missed here (wrong). All three previous focus items were drawn. D48's Expert Hour and the ledger move are on origin. The stayers item was retired with its runs queued and its launcher dead, and 3b9848300 relaunched them. The shared HEAD has forked again (2 ahead, 31 behind), on two commits of the stayers finding.

## 2026-10-14 — orientation: The one supplier fix that mattered reached origin, and in the same stretch the director's own guard on the save was found red

<!-- head: 58e1e89051db -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-14T11:21:28.356813+00:00; 9 commits, 0 substantive, since 2026-10-14T08:21:33.640236+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 0 supplier, 0 world, 0 both, 9 other.

## What the stretch meant

The one supplier fix that mattered reached origin, and in the same stretch the director's own guard on the save was found red. 87e9f4245 (merging e3b5ed01a) makes writer 1 read the unit-rate margin against what its strike priced for, and gives the save and the renewal cut one floor. So the retention grades can be taken on a floor that means what it says, and the regrade5 arms now run on it. My 05:20 sequencing error is corrected: the old-floor arms were stopped before they graded anything. Against the baseline, the stretch's one real reading is uncomfortable. 12aeea182 found that from 2019 the per-customer risk tiers and the flat price match net the same to the penny on 61109. So that seed's whole advantage for the tiers came before the cap, when the flat rule had no published default to match. Where a flat rule has a published anchor, inference has not yet shown it beats the flat rule, and regrade5 on writer 1's basis is the test of that. Worse, tests/simulation/test_a_save_is_not_paid_for_by_the_stayers.py is red at origin (2 of 8). Its precondition fails, so his 2026-10-08 condition is currently unreadable, the save has been live since 2026-10-10, and no census held the test. Until that is bisected, no save result can be called value created rather than transferred. The classifier counts 0 of 9 commits as substantive and the split as all other, because the supplier change arrived as a merge with no files of its own. The steer drifted. 3 of my 5 items were drawn. D48, named by its atom id, could not be drawn under anti-livelock, and the billing ledger was not drawn for a second stretch. Both are re-issued as slices with lanes. My 08:21 record also never reached origin (ae223deb0).

## 2026-10-14 — orientation: The stretch did the director's three knowledge pieces, and the one supplier fix that matters is built and not yet on origin

<!-- head: 58e1e89051db -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-14T08:21:33.640236+00:00; 13 commits, 6 substantive, since 2026-10-14T05:20:36.397267+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 1 world, 0 both, 11 other.

## What the stretch meant

The stretch did the director's three knowledge pieces, and the one supplier fix that matters is built and not yet on origin. e3b5ed01a makes writer 1 read the unit-rate margin against what its own strike priced for, rather than counting the standing charge as profit. It also gives the save and the renewal cut one floor (renewal_desk.pre_margin_unit_rate). At real inputs, a term that earned its GBP 2/MWh used to read 26% and take the full -5%. It now reads 1.01% against 1.01%, with no premium. surgical_land gated it green (EXIT 0), and then nothing promoted it. Its owner is gone and the commit is on no remote. Until it reaches origin, the thesis's central comparison, per-customer beating flat rules, still cannot be read in either direction. Its two seed-61109 arms (origin and fix) are running, and a handoff files their grade. Elsewhere the machine kept spending compute on the basis it had just declared wrong. The from-2019 price-match re-grade was correctly re-framed by 09c904ca1: before the cap there was no per-fuel default, so the match is graded from 2019 only. But it has restarted as eight 80-minute arms on the old floor, and its decision would have to be re-taken anyway. I stop it and re-take it behind the fix (focus two). That is my own sequencing error from 05:20. The census the director asked for first has not run. It has waited two hours in admission behind the 11.2 GB term-cost arm, which is also on the old basis but within about an hour of its end. The knowledge layer moved properly: P1's page and atoms (7c1ee032b), C34's sharing price (5d9218c43: the licence is silent on a savings-share fee, and the one computable GB split is 75/25), and D48's Expert Hour brief (a449e62da), all on origin. The split reads 1 supplier, 1 world and 11 other of 13. Of the previous focus, 1 of 3 was named-and-drawn: the price match moved through its continuation, and the billing-ledger item was never drawn, so that steer is drifting with Monday's publish five days out. Nothing went backwards. The project is one promotion away from being able to ask its central question honestly.

## 2026-10-14 — orientation: This stretch did not move a supplier result

<!-- head: d30dafffeb2f -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-14T05:20:36.397267+00:00; 11 commits, 2 substantive, since 2026-10-14T02:21:50.574673+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 0 supplier, 0 world, 1 both, 10 other.

## What the stretch meant

This stretch did not move a supplier result. It found why the supplier's results so far cannot be read, and that is worth more. d30dafffe settles P1 as definitional, not a loss-making price. The renewal floor charges the whole network allowance per kWh while the company also bills the standing charge that recovers its fixed share, so policy plus network on the floor (GBP 127-130/MWh) exceeds the cap's entire non-commodity unit allowance. Writer 1 then reads standing-charge revenue as margin (18-20% against an 8% target), discounts every renewal by the full 5%, and lands 21 of 21 on the floor. So every per-customer retention grade this week, the risk-tiers-beat-the-match decision included, was measured on a book the company prices from a mis-defined cost. The save is inert because of that, not because of its design. And the four-seed flat-rule baseline now running is on the same basis. Until writer 1's margin basis is fixed, 'per-customer beats flat rules' cannot be honestly answered, in either direction. That is focus one. c65f5b205 closed the price-match question too: no gate drops its offers. Before 2019 there was no cap, and so no ex-VAT default, so the match sat out three years. A re-grade from 2019 is running. Billing accuracy moved: the final-bill DD rule is on origin (84fb0d88d), graded, and changes no world response. That is correct billing, but it creates no value. The stranded demand-vector edit landed and moves no settlement figure (ac3612a6f). Monday's publish is no longer refused on it, but the site would still serve a 2026-10-05 billing ledger beside this week's pages (focus three). The split reads 0 supplier, 1 both and 10 other, and the both is real supplier code, the first in six stretches. Last focus was 4 of 4 drawn and 4 of 4 finished. Nothing went backwards, but the thesis's central comparison is not yet measurable.

## 2026-10-14 — orientation: The per-customer view won a decision this stretch, and the decision is weaker than its grade says

<!-- head: eb6b82e8e137 -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-14T02:21:50.574673+00:00; 10 commits, 2 substantive, since 2026-10-13T23:25:00.373796+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 0 supplier, 0 world, 0 both, 10 other.

## What the stretch meant

The per-customer view won a decision this stretch, and the decision is weaker than its grade says. On four fresh seeds, on a base carrying the week's floors, the floored risk tiers beat the price match paired 4 of 4 at the renewal cut. Under the tiers the company netted GBP 3.5k-8.6k a seed more and customers got more in cuts, so value was created on both sides, not transferred (d5ba38b12). But 5074f1d40 shows the match's 61109 loss is one commit's basis (d1e37f45c, ex-VAT): with it reverted the match nets -108 on 67 offers, not -4,264 on 13. eb6b82e8e then found that basis gives the match no default before 2019, so for twelve quarters the comparison was against a crippled rival. That is focus three. The same grade restates the deeper supplier fact. On these books, renewals sit at their own cost floor to the penny, so the save has nothing to offer. A book renewed at cost creates no margin to share, and whether that is a pricing defect or a floor counting the wrong cost is now P1 (focus four). The thesis's baseline, the per-customer arms against the flat-rule control on the director's book, still waits on the four-seed noise floor, near 17:00Z at the earliest. On integrity, c701d8605 is real progress: no run is published unless its imported bytes are its stamped commit's. Its first reading found that every run since 2026-09-24 imported an unlanded demand-vector edit, including the one on the live page and the held 6ab998ad7 run. So Monday's publish will be refused unless the edit is dispositioned (focus two). The split reads 0 supplier of 10 for the fifth stretch running, and no supplier code landed. The final-bill rule is in its gate for the third time (focus one). Of last focus, three items finished: the renewal re-grade, the run-bytes refusal and the floor's self-count fix (eb69dc942). The final-bill rule did not. Nothing went backwards, but supplier code is still not moving.

## 2026-10-14 — The renewal cut stays on risk tiers, and the noise floor stops refusing itself

<!-- head: 10d49dec98b7 -->

The renewal cut is decided, and a guard that made every noise floor refuse itself is fixed.

**Closed:**
- **Order 1's last open decision: the renewal cut stays on risk tiers.** The re-grade was
  pre-registered (668cb63db) and run on four fresh seeds at a base carrying this week's floors
  (d5ba38b12). The price match loses net on every seed, by GBP 3.5k-8.6k, because 9-15 more
  customers leave at renewal. It also gives customers less: GBP 100-300 of cuts a seed against
  770-1,080. Both sides of the value point the same way.
  - Held: predictions 1, 3 and 7. Refuted: 2, 6 and 8. Ungradable: 4 and 5, because the arm
    writes no no-offer cause.
  - The decision rule's "seed-spread" was undefined. I read it paired; across-seed it would
    have admitted the match.
  - My prediction 7 misattributed GBP 21.4 to the tiers, corrected beside it.
  - The match's offer count fell from 47 to 13 since d55598dd6. That is not attributed: more
    than one commit changed in between.
- **D48 L2 stands on the live site.** The deploy failed on a 57.7 MiB file; another lane fixed
  it. poesys.net now serves the figures L2 was recorded on (6/195, 7/113).
- **The noise-floor census counted its own launcher as an 11.2 GB leg** (eb69dc942).
  launch_long_job passes the leg's argv after `--`, so every floor launched through it refused
  itself: 22.4 GB needed on a 24 GB guest. The term-cost floors had refused since 22:10Z. The
  same admission-only hunk is applied in /var/tmp/se-termcost-arms. Floor A is now queued for
  memory behind another lane's two novat arms, not refusing itself.

**Wrong:** I re-issued the term-cost chain without checking that its next leg could start. It
could not, for the reason above, and I found that two hours later. For a re-issued chain,
check the next leg can start, not only the gap before it.

## 2026-10-14 — A run's stamp now has to match the code it imported, and the page's 2248e3baf figures did not

<!-- head: 4463fa84ceb4 -->

**Part 1, the 13:44Z run.** The publish of record the seat wanted to avoid did land. `ed3dadd9d` (2026-10-13 22:53 BST) put `run_output_2248e3baf_20261013T134447Z` on the page as 2248e3baf's figures. The seat judged that the run imported bytes that were on neither 2248e3baf nor origin. Its own finding said it could not check that after the 18:10Z fast-forward. **What I could measure, and it is wider:** `tools/demand_vector_coverage.py` in the shared tree has carried an unlanded code edit since 2026-09-24 (it drops `seasonal_swing` from the settlement choice's demand vector). Every run since then imported it, including the 13:44Z run and the 6ab998ad7 run (20:10Z). So the 2248e3baf stamp on the page names code that did not draw those figures. The figures are not known to be wrong; the stamp is.

**Why 6ab998ad7 is not on the page.** It finished at 23:05 and the publisher HELD it under the weekly window. The director ruled that window (Monday 04:00 London). The seat's "publish it as soon as it completes" conflicts with that ruling, and the ruling stands. The 6ab998ad7 run also ran the same unlanded bytes, so it is no cleaner a publish of record. I did not hand-edit `site/data/publish_provenance.json`, which the publisher regenerates on every publish. The caveat is recorded here and in the finding below.

**Part 2, landed.** sim-runner now reads, at launch, which files the run imports differ from the stamped commit (`code_closure.imports_off_commit`: `git diff` plus untracked files over the import closure; comment- or docstring-only diffs are named `prose_only` and not refused). The run writes that reading into `producing_commit.imports_off_commit`. The publisher refuses (rc 77, marker archived, paths named) a run whose list is non-empty or unmeasured. Artefacts that predate the reading pass, and the publisher logs that it did. The control file `tests/background/test_a_run_whose_imported_bytes_are_off_its_commit_is_not_published.py` was mutation-proven nine ways.

**What this costs on Monday.** While `tools/demand_vector_coverage.py` stays unlanded, Monday's publish will be refused. The seat must land the edit or refresh it to HEAD before Mon 2026-10-19 04:00: `WORKER_FINDING_EVERY_RUN_SINCE_09_24_IMPORTED_AN_UNLANDED_SETTLEMENT_CHOICE_AXIS_EDIT_AND_THE_PUBLISHER_NOW_REFUSES_IT_2026-10-14.md` (BLOCKING, H_harness). sim-runner was restarted at 23:35Z, after these bytes were on its disk, so it already runs this launcher. Any run it launched before then records "unmeasured" and is refused. The finding is archived under `docs/staging/done/` as the class gate requires, and listed as BLOCKING in `CLASS_UNCOMMITTED_AND_ORPHANED_WORK_2026-08-12.md`.

## 2026-10-14 — orientation: The thesis did not go backwards

## What the stretch meant

The thesis did not go backwards. The step back I flagged at 20:23 was not real. a0214b51d split the shared-149 fall after eaf49041b had pre-registered it. On the 83 accounts whose life path held across both arms and both runs, value minus control moved -293. The whole fall (-2,812 of -3,105) sits in 66 accounts whose bills differ between arms or runs, which is z = -0.47 against the per-account scatter. The term-cost base, my top pick, does not carry it, so by the rule fixed beforehand no revert run is warranted. That leaves the per-customer arm ahead of the flat-rule control on the whole book (5,244 to 4,652). Whether that lead is more than noise still waits on the four-seed noise floor, and that floor is now at risk. Floor leg a was refused three times on memory headroom (22:09, 22:15 and 23:15), while the renewal-cut arms held the box, and each time it wrote a REFUSAL into its artefact slot. The chain script running it only checks that a file exists, so it will read a refusal as a finished leg (focus three). The publish finally landed: ed3dadd9d at 21:53, deployed by hand at 22:59 after b1c3e4832 left the 57.7 MiB billing ledger out of the Pages upload. But it published the 13:44 run, the one my record said must not be the publish of record, because it imported stale bytes under stamp 2248e3baf. D48 then recorded L2 on those figures (ec0c00917). The level move is real on the page, but its evidence names a commit that did not produce it. Billing accuracy moved only through that level. The DD4b final-bill rule is back in a gate from its salvage tag (surgical_land pid 629834), and all four of its arms have now finished. The commit split reads 0 supplier of 13 for the fourth stretch running. That undercounts this stretch, though: the arms decomposition, the renewal cut's deciding pre-registration (668cb63db) and its eight arms are supplier work, filed as records. The steer bit: three of four items were drawn. The decomposition is done and leaves focus. P7 is now subsumed by the deciding re-grade on four fresh seeds, which is running, and grading it is focus two.

`None`. The retry at 13:44Z finished in 6929 s. **It is stamped 2248e3baf, which lacks 5f61c2262** (the SLC
20-24 ungraded-estimate fix; `merge-base --is-ancestor` says no). The item says the working copy of
`saas/reporting/compliance_scorecard_population.py` held origin's (5f61c2262) bytes while it ran, so the
`producing_commit` row says "2248e3baf drew every figure" about code it may not have run. That is a **new wrong
row**. I could not check the bytes after the fact, because the 18:10Z fast-forward restamped the file.
`resolved_at` is also the stamping time, not the launch time. Both are filed in one finding.

**The publish.** It passed the `tests/` gate in 1050 s, and the site lane refused it at 20:50Z with 72
failed and 7 errors. The cause was /tmp filling up, not a red test. `site/test_ia_register.py` copied the whole
`site/`, which the 774-household book has grown to 180 MB, into each of 18 tests, onto a shared 12 GB tmpfs.
Control: the same files pass 82/82 with TMPDIR on disk. With the default TMPDIR they error, and /tmp goes from
2.6 GB to 488 KB free. A worker tick landed the same fixture fix first (0d5304e98), so mine was dropped. What I
land is the control that the slimmer copy still carries every input the register reads.

**Not done.** No figures are on origin yet. The next publish is the 6ab998ad7 run that started at 20:10Z, or a
re-attempt of 134447Z. Either one needs this fix on the shared tree. A gate that reads a full tmpfs as red tests
is still possible from any other fixture. That is filed, not fixed.

Deck group 2 (reds at HEAD) and the shared-tree wedge, 17:00 to 19:15.

**Closed, by kind:**
- Reds at HEAD: four.
  - #16, #8 and #9 landed as cc5793d46: the test fixes, re-landed from a fresh base.

    change-of-tenancy window, and the arrears engine never bills a named payer for that.
    Verified 2 passed before landing.

  the tick log (aa7b2849e), so the next run of six-second rc=1 exits will name its cause.

    behind (7bc5cfac5).

  copies staged at origin's bytes, two identical untracked twins, and one subset copy, which is
  preserved. Another lane cleared the last two blockers in parallel; I stepped back once I saw
  it rather than race it on one index.

current tree. Reds #7, #12, #13 and #17 clear with that publish.

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-13T14:24:30.937972+00:00; 9 commits, 3 substantive, since 2026-10-13T11:22:03.695944+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 0 world, 1 both, 7 other.

## What the stretch meant

The supplier priced more honestly this stretch, but the one test of the thesis, the arms against the flat-rule baseline, has still not been read on current code, and no figure has reached the page for 184h. There were 9 commits, 3 substantive. The split was 1 supplier, 0 world, 1 both and 7 other, and every commit carried work. Two of the three previous focus items are finished, so they leave focus. (1) The 496-of-698 question was real, not a probe artefact. Writer 1 floored its discounts at the term cost without the capital charge, so it discounted into the capital band (c3bf385b9). 434d87587 floors it at the capital-inclusive cost the arm's base uses, with a control. (2) The price match now reads the published default ex VAT at one seam (d1e37f45c). But the item's DONE also asked for 82e84e4a4's P7 (-3,089 against the tiers on seed 61109) to be re-read on the corrected basis, and I find no re-read on origin, so that half is re-issued (focus three). The hedge's booking price was measured to move only the desk's own book. Settled margin is identical to the penny, so the 2026-10-12 item's WHY (that it flattered every margin) was false. What it did fix is a trading book that reported +GBP 6.1k of hedge P&L that settlement never contained, and credit exposure understated by about 30% (4490454bf). The arms re-take on the term-cost base is pre-registered with eight predictions (8b0cbf04c). Leg 1 is running (termcost-arms-leg1), and its grade is a continuation embargoed to 17:15. So the honest pricing is now in place and its grade is in flight, which is the right order. What went backwards is the publish, and the cause was misread. 05f9f3347 found that the publisher gates a checkout of the SHARED HEAD (2248e3baf, 52 behind origin). The HEAD cannot fast-forward because the shared index holds a staged pile that differs from origin, and the finding stood down because that pile was 'in the console seat's landing sequence'. I read the pile this orientation, and that premise is spent. The sequence finished: 2d864882e, c6317ca9f, 61c122683, 04913b693 and 434d87587 are all on origin. The staged copies of company/billing/dd_review.py, simulation/dd_balance_book.py, the DD tests and the DD knowledge page are byte-equal to versions in origin's own history that origin has since superseded. The staged value_based_renewal.py lacks 04913b693's term-cost base. So the pile is stale predecessors, not unlanded work, apart from at most two DD records and one finding addendum. Worse, the publish run now in flight (pid 357420, 13:44, stamped 2248e3baf) imports those stale working copies. Its figures would come from code that is on no commit (wrong). Focus one clears the pile and gets a run on origin's bytes to the page. The previous focus did reach the draw (3 named, 3 drawn).

## 2026-10-13 — orientation: The director's DD design is now wired and measured, and two pricing questions now decide whether the next baseline comparison means anything

<!-- head: 2248e3baf244 -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-13T11:22:03.695944+00:00; 9 commits, 4 substantive, since 2026-10-13T08:24:43.731101+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 0 world, 3 both, 5 other.

## What the stretch meant

The director's DD design is now wired and measured, and two pricing questions now decide whether the next baseline comparison means anything. There were 9 commits, 4 substantive, split 1 supplier, 0 world, 3 both and 5 other, and 2 changed nothing. c6317ca9f gives the DD review the term end and the company's own forward. On the single-levy book the split closes GBP 4.8k of the 2018-06 review lag, more than the filed prediction, and the default stays as it was, with its reason recorded. So the previous focus two is finished and leaves. 5c137eb5b floors the risk-tier retention cut at its own cost floor. 82e84e4a4 graded the fresh-seed recount: held notices below the floor fell from 23 of 27 to 4 of 28, with 0 offers. 5f61c2262 fixed the None that killed the publish, and 3a692ad58 landed the 145 banners. Against the thesis, the supplier is close to pricing honestly but has not shown it yet. 2473321d6 moved every priced renewal onto the term's own cost, by a median of 2.61 GBP/MWh. Its probe also says the struck rate before the value arm sits below that cost on 496 of 698 renewals. If that is real, writer 1 is selling under cost on most of the book, and any arms-vs-flat-rule figure taken now measures that defect, not inference. So the arms re-take waits on that answer (focus one). The price match is still graded on an inc-VAT default against ex-VAT renewals. That makes 82e84e4a4's -3,089 for the price match against the tiers a number about the bug (focus two). It was not drawn because the tiers-floor worktree held growth_desk.py, and that worktree is now gone. Of the three previous focus items, two were drawn. The DD wiring is finished. The publish fix is on origin, and a publish run started at 11:24 (pid 2607003), but no figures have reached origin for 181h, so it stays in focus as a landing, not a build. One thing went backwards that I had told the lanes not to do: a third recount arm was launched at 09:32 against the director's 07:10 instruction (wrong). The executor did honour "land before build": four of the substantive commits were landings of finished work.

## 2026-10-13 — orientation: Three of the four supplier changes the director named this morning are on origin, and the publish is not

<!-- head: 2248e3baf244 -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-13T08:24:43.731101+00:00; 20 commits, 6 substantive, since 2026-10-13T05:23:54.698074+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 0 supplier, 0 world, 2 both, 18 other.

## What the stretch meant

Three of the four supplier changes the director named this morning are on origin, and the publish is not. There were 20 commits, 6 substantive, split 0 supplier, 0 world, 2 both and 18 other, and 4 changed nothing. 81c129fe8 puts the capital target at GBP 115 dated per C14, so the capital wrong row is corrected and retired in triage (d73cc0d8f). 61c122683 books each hedge at the market's own point-in-time forward quote, not the company's belief. That removes an advantage that came from how the model was built rather than from inference, and its control is in its gate (surgical_land pid 4138581). The director's DD rule is in its gate (pid 4089567), and the risk-tier retention floor is in its gate too (pid 4052657). The recount my last focus asked for (95b3a38d2) answered its question. Writer 1's floor fixed most of the below-cost renewals, and 2 of 8 held notices on seed 61109 still renew under their own cost, both through the risk-tier retention cut, which runs after the class check. So the save still cannot fire. Against the thesis, we are now one landing and one wiring away from a supplier whose renewals and hedges are priced honestly. Until then a per-customer decision graded against the flat-rule baseline would still be measuring the model's construction. A new defect bears on that: the price match compares an inc-VAT default with ex-VAT renewal rates, so both desks under-offer by about 5%. That is the VAT class again, in a sixth place (focus three). One thing went backwards, and I read it wrongly last time. The publish run I reported as running died at 05:35 on one None after nearly two hours, and nothing filed it. No publish has landed for 178h. The box is held again by arms, three of them admitted after the director said to stop admitting them. His pace instruction (about 8 points a day, land before build) is followed in what the lanes picked, which was mostly landings, but not in what they ran. Of the previous four focus items, three were drawn. The recount is finished and leaves focus. The hedge is landed and its control is with its holder. The DD rule is in its gate. The mover's destination weather was not drawn, and under the director's pace it goes to not_now.

## 2026-10-13 — orientation: One supplier change reached origin this stretch, and the supplier result it bears on was measured on code that predates the fix

<!-- head: 34f6e20d280a -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-13T05:23:54.698074+00:00; 22 commits, 8 substantive, since 2026-10-13T02:22:20.229260+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 1 supplier, 1 world, 0 both, 20 other.

## What the stretch meant

One supplier change reached origin this stretch, and the supplier result it bears on was measured on code that predates the fix. There were 22 commits, 8 of them substantive, split 1 supplier, 1 world and 20 other, and 7 changed nothing (merges). The balance is still not the director's. 04913b693 makes the value arm read its margin from the term's own cost instead of the rate writer 1 left. b234e27bd graded the save and the renewal cut on fresh seeds 61109-61112. The save never fired, because on 23 of 27 loss notices the renewal rate already sat below the company's own cost floor. The price-match cut lost net on every seed, so the cut stays on risk tiers. That is the most important supplier fact of the week: a book renewing below its own cost has no room to make any per-customer decision. But the arms ran at ed668c733, and 03a0b66da, which floors writer 1's renewal discounts at the desk's cost, is not an ancestor of it. Neither is 04913b693. So the P1 the finding ranks for next week may already be answered on origin, and nothing asked. That is the carried hold-premise defect again, and focus two re-asks it on one seed before anyone builds against it. 5cdaca020 (world) makes the in-loop DD review read the supplier's own bills, not true consumption, which is the epistemic wall applied to the DD tail. Three finished supplier changes are still not on origin. The director's DD rule has been unlanded for about 24 hours, the last 1.8 of them under a draw that landed nothing. The hedge at the market's quote is staged in the shared index and was not drawn. The GBP 115 capital fix is in its gate now (surgical_land pid 1654714). The shared index also carries about 150 staged paths from other lanes, so a landing without a pathspec would sweep them. The weekly publish is running at 2f5c926dc (run_annual_report pid 331991, 1h47m) after 175 hours with none. That has not landed yet, so the publish error stays open. value-arm-measure-61001 died at launch with exit 1, and the same measurement now runs by hand from /tmp (pid 1370055) outside the launch register. Of the previous five focus items, two were drawn and none landed under its own name. Against the thesis we are not behind on inference. We are behind on landing: the per-customer levers exist, and the baseline comparison cannot be trusted while renewals may price under cost and finished billing work sits in the tree.

## What went wrong

**Reading: 59% at 17:00 Tuesday.** 41 points remain to Monday 04:00. Keeping a 6-point reserve leaves **35 to spend**. The conversion holds at **USD 26.6 a point** (`tools/tick_burn_rate.py --points`, now on three readings). The 8-a-day line is dropped, as the director asked: spend runs as fast as the most valuable clear-down allows, in value-per-point order.

The unattended lanes (worker ticks on Opus, the executor, the orienting seat) will spend about **21 of the 35** by Monday at today's rate. They draw from this same deck, so their points are clearing capacity, not overhead. This seat has about **14**.

## What the stretch meant

No supplier-only commit reached origin this stretch. There were 13 commits, 2 substantive, split 0 supplier, 1 world, 1 both and 11 other, and 5 of the 13 changed nothing. The one supplier change is real. 03a0b66da stops writer 1 discounting renewal fixes below the cost the desk struck over. No per-customer decision has been graded against the flat-rule baseline on a frozen world in a way that measures the decision. The mover offer was graded on four fresh seeds (42b39b8d6), and five of six predictions hold. But only 7 of 23 followers were supplied at the new home, and its net rises with that count, so the grade mostly measured the weather store. That is focus four. On the steer, of five focus items only the capital fix moved. Its GBP 115 copies and the C14 dating are finished but uncommitted in the shared tree, under the interactive seat's claim. The director's DD design, H45 and the salvage item were never drawn, because the executor spent the stretch on continuations. The DD design goes first now. The machine's worst drift is the publish. Nothing has reached origin for 169h, and sim-runner deferred every cycle tonight on an exhausted memory budget as new grade jobs were admitted. My last record said that would clear within the hour, and that was wrong (new row). Focus three reserves the box for the publish, so the next job queues behind it. The director asked tonight whether the long jobs were broken. They are not broken, but nothing was ordering them. Wrong: all twelve carried rows stay open, one new seat row is added, and last stretch's three corrected rows drop.

<!-- head: 31e639bcda9e -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-12T17:21:15.224259+00:00; 23 commits, 7 substantive, since 2026-10-12T14:21:20.412293+00:00).*

## What the stretch meant

For the first time in five stretches, supplier code reached origin. There were 23 commits, 7 substantive, split 1 supplier, 2 world, 1 both and 19 other. 441994e17 moved the DD review, the ledger's dunning notices and the portfolio margin book into company code behind doors, and the run loop now asks the renewal desk through one typed record. The regrade predictions record that move as proven book-identical. 5187cb21a has the default-tariff segment hedge and price its mover offer off the company's own forward, not the world's. The world kept to freeze-then-solve. 553d7c855 froze the household payment world on one payment truth with blind predictions that held. Its >91-day arrears stock matches Ofgem's, and its write-off flow undershoots the record about 5-7x, carried as a named gap. The root blocker of the last three stretches is gone: origin_reconcile put the shared checkout on origin at 15:44, and HEAD is level. But no publish has landed (163h). sim-runner defers every cycle on the memory budget the interactive seat's grade jobs hold. That is a choice of what to run, not a fault. Against the thesis, the gap has still not closed. No per-customer decision has been graded against the flat-rule baseline on a frozen world. The nearest is B8 Q5: a99685b68 recommended the price match as the standing renewal cut on three seeds. 31e639bcd then found it declines 71-77 renewals per seed, because the rate chain's learning premium prices fixes below the desk's own cost floor. That is a pricing defect under the lever, and it is queued as a continuation. Two things went backwards. The GBP 115 capital fix I reported in its gate at 14:21 left no commit anywhere. Its only copy is uncommitted in /tmp/wt_capt115 with a dead owner, the same shape that lost the provision fix this morning. And the stop-board defect is still live: the arrears400 run printed 'company provision could not be read: no run has installed a DD stop-notice board'. Three of the provision grade's four members crashed at the grade step. On the steer: of four focus items, the brief counts one drawn. The checkout was spent by origin_reconcile before it was drawn (f8dfb8951). The DD-review move was done by the interactive seat (441994e17). Capital and provision did not land. Work still reaches the supplier mainly through the interactive seat, not the lane. Wrong is graded against the triage register. The six rows 1a3800d18 gave a fold or accept fate drop out: double levy, b7s7, four principles, the publish behind origin, the steer and the reaped worktree. Their owners hold them now. One fold's class recurred: /tmp/wt_capt115 is a second dead-owner dirty worktree, so focus four builds the mechanism.

## 2026-10-12 — Clear-the-decks, first stretch: canon v4 installed and aligned, worker ticks on the advisor trial, the shared tree unwedged, four reds cleared

<!-- head: 002d37e422a2 -->

**Spent since the 40% reading (Monday 14:00):** about USD 93 weighted, so about 5 points at ~USD 19 a point (corrected calibration, 99a2ff7a1). That is this session and its agents (USD 85; the world lane is USD 38 of it) plus at least USD 7.5 of unattended turns. Inside the ~9 a day the week allows.

**Closed, by kind**

- *Pacing (the biggest lever):* the worker ticks run on Sonnet 5 with an Opus 5.5 advisor in a dated window to 19 Oct (99a2ff7a1). The stop rule was filed before the first tick. The first trial tick ran on Sonnet 5 with the advisor attached (advisor_message iterations on Opus 5.5 in its transcript), so the precondition is met. Along the way, tools/tick_burn_rate.py was found counting every message about 2.2x; it is fixed, and the calibration is corrected beside its claim.
- *Canon v4, steps 1-4 and part of 2 and 5:*

  - CLAUDE.md quotes canon, and G5 is in code, narrowed to its words (6a64ec275);
  - the model on a page, the pitch, the human simulation layer and the overview are aligned, with two new startup anchors (002d37e42);

  - the eight for_the_director rows were already answered by the seat's 12:28 record;
  - C34 ranks on joint value with both floors (eeb38abc3);
  - grid losses have their own line at BEIS/DESNZ factors for all ten years (ebad187e8).
- *Reds at HEAD:* a census of the 18 found 3 green again and 2 environmental. Four are fixed (252e20edb): the decision probe's keyword call, a refusal test keyed to its concept, and two alarm-census rows.
- *Stale worktrees:* 168 down to 119, each archived first (/var/tmp/worktree-archive-20261012, 78 MB). The 4 that held unlanded commits are kept as refs and bundles. One generated docs mirror was not archived (a tar flag-order bug); its run was already published (f4bcaa6f2).

**Raised to him:** C34 still advises nobody at realistic inputs, because our floor binds in all 18 cases. Recommended: pair a value-creating action with a price that shares the value (an atom for next week).

## 2026-10-12 — orientation: For the fourth stretch running, no supplier code reached origin

<!-- head: 47e8e6993c6a -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-12T14:21:20.412293+00:00; 14 commits, 6 substantive, since 2026-10-12T11:21:01.669153+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 0 supplier, 1 world, 0 both, 13 other.

## What the stretch meant

For the fourth stretch running, no supplier code reached origin. There were 14 commits, 6 substantive, split 0 supplier, 1 world and 13 other. Most of what landed was governance the director asked for. Canon v4 is installed in his words (78afa32c7), and CLAUDE.md now quotes it and holds the reserved actions to G5's one list (6a64ec275). The world kept to freeze-then-solve. 87ee5a3bc re-froze the payment world on one payment truth with blind predictions first, and every result fell inside its range. 0e24b302d honestly refused to freeze the DD shock at its range ends, because it answers only 10 of the world's 299 material DD rises and none in 2022-23. That is a real limit on the first supplier payment lever: a DD review graded against this world cannot yet be hurt by a shock in the year that matters most. Against the thesis, the gap has not narrowed. No per-customer decision has yet been graded against the flat-rule baseline on a frozen world. Two supplier pieces are close. The GBP 115 capital target is in its gate now (pid 2714123), and C34's joint-value ranking is committed in /var/tmp/se-canon2, where it finds that at realistic inputs our no-loss floor still refuses every advice action. That is a finding against the thesis's per-customer claim, not for it. One thing went backwards. The movers' final-bill grade and the stop-board fix that makes the company's provision readable at all were finished. They were lost when /var/tmp/se-provgrade was reaped uncommitted. The defect is still live on origin, so every published provision still reads 'unavailable'. The shared checkout is still the root blocker. It is 84 behind, three files still stop the fast-forward, no publish has landed for about 160 hours, and worker-tick is not yet running the model-tier change the director approved. Of my 11:21 focus, one item was drawn (the capital landing). The canon item and half the checkout item were done by the interactive seat with no draw, and the provision item was refused on a holder that is doing different work in the same file. The canon item is finished and leaves focus.

## 2026-10-12 — Clear-the-decks week: the calibration (~USD 43 a point), what 55 points buys, and what will not fit

<!-- head: b1113bc543f0 -->

*Interactive delivery seat, Monday 2026-10-12 ~14:00 BST. Director's reading: 40% of the weekly allowance used; the week runs to the reset at Monday 19 October 04:00 BST, about 55 points, ~9 a day. Canon P12 as amended today: I pace myself to land at about 95% at the reset. This is a clear-the-decks week (a dated exception to P6).*

## The calibration
`tools/tick_burn_rate.py --days 7`: last week's turns cost ~USD 4,230 at list-price weighting -- seat executor 1,063 (165 turns, 79% landed), worker ticks 1,255 (207 turns, 74% landed), the orienting seat 180 (53 turns), this interactive session 1,726. That week took the director to ~98% by Saturday, so **one point is roughly USD 43 weighted** (plus or minus ~30%: the windows do not align exactly). 55 points is about USD 2,370. **Corrected later the same day:** the tool summed one message's usage once per content block it was written in (11,078 rows for 5,151 messages, ~2.2x). Fixed, the same `--days 7` read is ~USD 1,900, so **one point is ~USD 19 weighted and 55 points ~USD 1,070**. Both sides of every per-point figure below were read in the same inflated unit, so the point budgets stand; the dollar figures do not.

**The problem:** at last week's rates the unattended lanes alone (executor, ticks, orientation) spend ~8.3 points a day -- the whole week's budget -- before any interactive work. So the week only fits if the mix changes:
- worker ticks onto the approved advisor trial (Sonnet main, Opus advisor; ruled 2026-10-12): estimated -50 to -60% on ~4.2 pts/day;
- the interactive seat at ~2-2.5 pts/day: Sonnet/Haiku subagents for census, search and batch fates; Opus only for code and judgment; one or two agents at a time, not four;
- executor and orientation unchanged (~4.1 pts/day), pointed at the deck through focus.
That is ~8 pts/day, ~53 for the week. I re-estimate at each reading.

## What 55 points buys (rough, in points)
1. **Payment work in flight, ~9-11:** finish the household-world freeze (~1, in flight); the expected-loss provision against held-back loss on the frozen world (~1.5); re-grade the save, mover offer and renewal cut on fresh seeds across the ranges (~2-3; compute-heavy, token-light); the typed seam record for run-loop inputs and the DD review and dunning out of world files (~4-5).
2. **Canon v4, ~14-18:** install, align, banner, close the eight rows, report (~4); the rulings in code -- C34 joint value with no-loss floors, the pricing-arm check, the company reading its own holdout, the T&D-loss line, the time unit in C31, the capital target from 31 Mar 2025 at GBP 115 measured, retiring epoch gates, NTFY under G8 (~8-10); the canon-against-canon check and the two anchors (~2); the twelve owed items in §15 (~2-4 where evidence exists; more where an item is a build).
3. **Clear the decks, ~18-24:** reds at HEAD, broken controls, dead runs, stale worktrees first (~3; highest value per point); the known-issues triage under the 7 October rule (~2); the staging backlog -- ~200 in the root and 123 in progress, one fate each -- batched by rule (superseded, stale, already done) with a cheap model and judgment only where a rule cannot decide (~10-14); the owed list overlaps item 2.

**Total ~41-53 points.** It fits if the pacing changes hold.

## What will not fit
- A one-by-one Opus reading of all ~323 staging documents: the backlog is fated in batches by rule, and documents a rule cannot decide go to the back, ranked, or take "accept with a stated reason".
- Any owed item or ruling that is a new capability: building retention from published trials (C8, the save and retention levers) and anything else new become atoms for next week, as directed.
- The supplier payment engine: it opens next week.

For the third stretch running, no supplier code reached origin: 4 commits, 1 substantive, split 0 supplier, 1 world and 3 other. That is not because nothing was built. The supplier work is finished and STRANDED in three places. The GBP 115 capital figure gated green as 09fca096c and was refused at promotion only because origin moved during its gate, and its owner is dead (/tmp/wt_capt115). The movers' final-bill grade has sat uncommitted in /var/tmp/se-provgrade for 22 hours. The best-deal gap, moved from a world file into the commons, is in its gate now (59411d983). The world side followed the director's freeze-then-solve order exactly. f49c13405 froze household payment behaviour with predictions filed before its low and high runs (the sha256 of the block as filed, results below it, one refuted count attributed by a one-variable run). That closes my open row on unfiled predictions. 62596685a lets the write-offs come from the same payment truth, shipped off. So the precondition for the thesis's first payment lever now exists: a frozen world against which a supplier DD review can be graded. But no lever has moved into the company yet, and the thesis claim, beating a flat-rule supplier by inference, is no nearer a grade than it was at 08:20. B8 Q5's base seed is graded (611622ef9): the price match offers 49 where the tiers offer 110, for a net of +GBP 905, with P4 refuted. All four seed arms finished at 10:58, and their grade is a continuation that opens at 11:30. The director answered every open concern by agreeing all fourteen canon-v4 decisions (e89a7728a). All eight rows close below. Three of his answers create supplier work: C34 ranks on joint value, the company's own holdout becomes readable, and the capital target binds from 31 March 2025. The last is folded into focus two, and the rest follow his own sequencing (not_now). Two things went wrong. My 08:20 focus did not reach the draw (new wrong row). And the shared checkout is now 69 behind origin and still cannot fast-forward, so no publish has landed for about 157 hours. sim-runner is spending 2.6 GB on another 47e8e6993 run whose publish will hit the same wall. That stays first.

## 2026-10-12 — orientation: For the second stretch running the supplier did not move, and the director cannot see that, because nothing new has reached his page in 154 hours

<!-- head: 47e8e6993c6a -->

*Written by the orientation seat from its own record (2026-10-12T08:20:50.153051+00:00; 6 commits, 3 substantive, since 2026-10-12T05:23:33.161860+00:00).*

Commit split (product code by path): 0 supplier, 3 world, 0 both, 3 other.

## What the stretch meant

For the second stretch running the supplier did not move, and the director cannot see that, because nothing new has reached his page in 154 hours. There were 6 commits, 3 substantive, split 0 supplier, 3 world and 3 other. The world work followed his 2026-10-12 order exactly. With f853cd2ff, the household payment world now gives all four answers he ruled must exist before the payment engine is graded: an arrangement offer, early contact (9ca9624fc), cancelling the mandate with the route to prepayment (1cadad9b5), and a changed DD amount or date (3a35fbc8f). Each is answered from the household's own money and each ships off. That is the right order, but it is still world. The thesis claim, that the company beats a flat-rule supplier by inference, is no nearer a grade until that world is frozen at its range ends and a supplier lever is moved into the company and graded against it. Focus three and four are those two steps. The previous focus all reached the draw. The four-principles audit is on origin, and the director has its answer (b05429544, NTFY yzf66zm0kGie). Last stretch I put this down to the allowance without evidence, and I correct that beside it: I cannot yet say what causes it. Nothing went backwards in the model.
